title: Nrcm's Codestorm - 2K26
description: About CODESTORM - 2K26 Narsimha Reddy Engineering College (NRCM) presents CODESTORM - 2K26 , the ultimate 36-hour National Level Hackathon designed to bring together passionate students, developers, innovators, and problem-solvers to build impactful solutions for real-world challenges. Under the theme "Build the Future… Break the Limits" , CODESTORM - 2K26 focuses on innovation, creativity, technical excellence, and practical problem-solving . Participants will work on real-world challenges released on-spot and will have 36 hours to ideate, design, develop, test, and present their solutions. Compete with talented participants and showcase your skills for a total prize pool of ₹2,00,000! HealthTech & MedAI Technology-driven solutions for better healthcare. FinTech & Blockchain Innovations in finance, digital payments, and blockchain. Smart Cities & IoT Connected solutions for smarter, safer cities. Green Tech & Energy Sustainable solutions for energy and the environment. Agritech & Rural Innovation Technology for smarter agriculture and rural development. Transportation & Logistics Innovations for smarter mobility and efficient logistics. Open Innovation ( Wildcard ) Build innovative solutions beyond the defined domains. Eligibility & Team Rules Team Size: 3 to 5 members per team. Open to All: Students from any department and year can participate. Inter-College Teams: Teams comprising students from different colleges are allowed and encouraged. Participants must complete the official registration process through the NRCM portal. Event Timeline Registration Deadline: 25-09-2026 | Before 09:00 PM Reporting & Registration: 30-09-2026 | Before 10:00 AM On-Spot Challenge Release: 30-09-2026 | 10:30 AM Hackathon Begins: 30-09-2026 | 10:30 AM 36-Hour Hackathon: 30-09-2026 to 01-10-2026 Final Submission & Results: 01-10-2026 | 04:00 PM onwards Facilities & Benefits 36-Hour Offline Hackathon: Build and compete at the NRCM campus. Technical Support: Expert mentoring and guidance throughout the hackathon. Infrastructure: High-speed Wi-Fi and facilities to support development. Food & Refreshments: Meals, snacks, and refreshments for participants. Rest Facilities: Dedicated rest arrangements during the hackathon. Recognition: Participation certificates and exciting prizes for winning teams. Career Opportunities: Top-performing participants may get opportunities for internships and career prospects. Prize Pool Total Prize Pool: ₹2,00,000 The best-performing teams will be recognized and rewarded for their innovation, technical implementation, feasibility, and presentation . Judging Criteria Solutions will be evaluated based on: Innovation & Creativity Technical Implementation Real-World Impact Feasibility & Scalability Presentation & Pitch Important Rules Build from Scratch: Solutions must be developed during the hackathon. Pre-built or pre-developed solutions are not permitted. On-Spot Challenges: Challenge statements will be released during the event. No Prior Idea Submission: Participants do not need to submit an idea or abstract before the hackathon. Offline Event: The hackathon will be conducted at the Narsimha Reddy Engineering College campus, Kompally, Hyderabad. Venue Narsimha Reddy Engineering College (NRCM) Maisammaguda (V), Kompally Hyderabad - 500100, Telangana Build the Future. Break the Limits. Bring your team, solve real-world challenges, build something impactful, and compete for ₹2,00,000 in prizes at CODESTORM - 2K26! Register through the official website: https://nrcmec.org/CS2026

title: Data Analytics Hackathon
description: This is a build-and-analysis-focused Data Analytics Hackathon designed for students, aspiring analysts, data professionals, and problem-solvers who want to turn raw data into meaningful insights and actionable recommendations. What You'll Do: On 27th September , 11 AM to 12 PM (IST) participants will work with a real-world dataset provided by the organizers and perform an end-to-end data analysis by: Understanding the business problem and dataset. Cleaning, transforming, and preparing the data. Exploring patterns, trends, and relationships. Performing quantitative and statistical analysis. Building meaningful visualizations and dashboards. Identifying key insights and actionable recommendations. Presenting your analysis and findings. The challenge is centered around using data to solve real-world problems by turning raw datasets into clear insights and data-driven decisions. By the end of the Hackathon, you'll have a complete analysis project that can be showcased in your portfolio, discussed during interviews, or further developed into a real-world analytics solution. Who Can Participate? Individuals and teams are welcome. Recommended team size: Max 2 members & Individualy can also Participate. Beginners and experienced analysts can participate. Participants can use Python, SQL, Excel, Power BI, Tableau, and other analytics tools. Project Requirements: Every team must: Perform the analysis using the dataset provided during the event. Clearly document the analysis process and methodology. Explain the problem statement, approach, findings, and recommendations. Submit a complete and functional analysis with supporting visualizations. Submission Checklist: To complete your submission, provide: Final analysis report or presentation. Dashboard and/or data visualizations. Source code/notebook or analysis file, where applicable. Brief explanation of the methodology and key findings. Key insights and actionable recommendations. Rules & Judging Criteria: Event Rules: Participants must use the dataset provided by the organizers. Pre-built analyses or previously completed projects are not permitted. External tools, libraries, and publicly available resources may be used. Any form of plagiarism or unauthorized copying will result in disqualification. Participants must disclose the use of AI tools in their analysis or submission. All submissions must be completed and submitted before the official deadline. Evaluation Areas: Projects will be assessed based on: Data cleaning and preparation. Analytical approach and problem-solving. Quality and accuracy of insights. Data visualization and storytelling. Depth of analysis. Business relevance and actionable recommendations. Overall presentation and completeness. Turn data into insights, uncover the story behind the numbers, and show how analytics can drive better decisions.
prize: Winner: ₹5000 | 1st Runner-Up: ₹3000 | 2nd Runner-Up: ₹1500 | Kind Prize Worth: ₹50000

title: Dogfood | 72-Hour Hackathon
description: About the Hackathon Dogfood 2026 is a 72-hour online hackathon built around one challenge: build the platform that will judge you. Hackathon Raptors has run 35+ hackathons across 85+ countries, and this challenge comes directly from the problems encountered while running them. Registration, team formation, submissions, eligibility, judge assignment, scoring, normalization, results, certificates, and archiving all form one complex data pipeline. Your challenge is to build a modern, open-source, self-hostable hackathon submission and judging platform that handles this entire lifecycle. Everyone builds the same product against the same published specification. There are no tracks. This is not a hackathon where you build a demo of a platform. We are asking you to build ours. The winning project will be forked, self-hosted, and put into production for Hackathon Raptors events. You keep ownership of your work, and the project remains open source. The platform must run locally with a single command. A working submission should start with docker compose up , seed itself with the provided fixture data, and work without a cloud account, hosted database, authentication provider, external API, or network connection. Stay Updated All announcements, specification releases, rule clarifications, fixture data, acceptance suite updates, submission instructions, FAQs, and live support happen through the official Hackathon Raptors Discord. Discord Server Invite: Join the Hackathon Raptors Discord Event Website: dogfoodhack.com Organizer: raptors.dev Why Participate Hackathon platforms have largely converged on the same basic features. The interesting engineering problems are what happens underneath them: fair judging, role isolation, score normalization, abuse prevention, reliable data flows, APIs, and software that an organizer can actually self-host and operate. Participants will get to: Build a complete hackathon platform from registration through results. Work on authentication, authorization, teams, submissions, galleries, dashboards, and exports. Design backend-enforced role isolation and permission systems. Build weighted and configurable judging rubrics. Solve cross-judge score normalization. Design fairer community voting and anti-abuse mechanisms. Work with assignment algorithms, ranking systems, and statistical methods. Build an API-first, self-hostable platform. Practice production-oriented DevOps and local deployment. Create software that may actually be used in future Hackathon Raptors events. Demonstrate engineering judgment, technical depth, and ability to ship under constraints. AI coding assistants are allowed and expected. The challenge is not whether AI helped. It is whether you can ship, test, explain, and defend what you built. Eligibility Dogfood is open to: Students. Software developers. Engineers. Researchers. Professionals. Open-source contributors. Full-stack developers. Backend and API engineers. Frontend and design-system builders. Data and algorithms enthusiasts. Security engineers. DevOps and self-hosting enthusiasts. Anyone interested in building serious software, from any country. Team Size 1-4 members. Solo participation is allowed. Teams of 2-4 are recommended. Cross-college teams are allowed. Cross-disciplinary teams are allowed. Event Format The hackathon runs entirely online for 72 hours. Every team builds the same product: an open-source, self-hostable hackathon submission and judging platform. During the event, teams are expected to: Design and implement the platform against the published specification. Build the required core functionality. Implement judging, scoring, normalization, and role isolation. Test the platform against edge cases and failure scenarios. Run the provided acceptance suite against their implementation. Document the architecture, data model, judging system, and technical decisions. Verify that the project can run locally without hosted-service dependencies. Prepare a working demonstration. Submit the required source code, documentation, acceptance report, and demo video. Tier Ladder There are four tiers. Everyone builds against the same specification, and teams are evaluated based on how far they climb and how correctly they implement each tier. T1 - Core: Authentication and sessions, participant/judge/organizer/admin roles, event creation, configurable dates, tracks and prizes, team formation through invite links, project submission with draft and edit functionality, deadline enforcement, and a searchable public gallery. T1 is the minimum requirement to be judged. T2 - Judging: Judge invitation and assignment, batch or algorithmic assignment, weighted and configurable judging rubrics, backend-enforced role isolation, judge progress dashboards, cross-judge score normalization, and CSV export throughout the workflow. T3 - Public: Configurable community voting, comments, hidden results during voting, randomized project ordering, rate limiting, duplicate detection, audit trails, or an alternative voting mechanism that can be technically defended. T4 - Stretch: REST API and webhooks covering UI actions, certificate and record generation, signed and publicly verifiable judge participation records, an embeddable gallery widget, and bulk import and export. A clean, correct T2 is better than a broken T4. Tier claims are verified through the acceptance suite, not through the README. What Counts as Done Your project must produce a working portal from a single command. docker compose up must start a seeded, working platform locally. The project must not depend on: Hosted databases. Authentication-as-a-service. External APIs. Cloud accounts. Proprietary services. Network connectivity. The acceptance suite will run against your build and produce a tier-by-tier pass report. The acceptance report must be included in your public repository. If the project cannot run on a laptop with the network turned off, it cannot be adopted. AI Tools AI coding assistants are allowed and expected, including Claude Code, Cursor, Aider, GitHub Copilot, local AI models, and others. AI usage itself is not scored. We evaluate whether the final implementation works, whether the architecture and data model are sound, and whether the team can explain and defend the software it built. What You Need to Submit Each team must submit: Public GitHub repository. OSI-approved open-source license. Working implementation. docker compose up setup that starts a seeded portal. acceptance-report.txt . README.md . ARCHITECTURE.md . DATA-MODEL.md . JUDGING.md . Tests. 5-minute demo video showing one complete event lifecycle. Your JUDGING.md should explain your judge assignment strategy, scoring methodology, normalization method, and the reasoning behind your approach. Your ARCHITECTURE.md should explain the system design and major technical decisions. Your DATA-MODEL.md should document the schema and import/export paths. Judging Criteria Projects will be evaluated on: Tier Completion & Correctness - 40%: How far up the tier ladder the project reaches, verified by the acceptance suite. Correctness matters more than feature count, and honest gap reporting is rewarded. Judging Integrity - 25%: How well the platform handles role isolation, judge assignment, score normalization, auditability, and voting abuse. The judging system must be technically defensible. Adoptability & Operability - 20%: Whether Hackathon Raptors could realistically run the software. One-command startup, seeded data, documentation, migration paths, clean licensing, and self-hosting all matter. Code Quality & Innovation - 15%: Code quality, maintainability, schema design, architecture, and the technical decisions that make the project stand out. Bonus Challenges Optional bonus challenges are available: Normalization Proof (+5): Implement cross-judge normalization and demonstrate its effect using the provided fixture data. Pairwise Mode (+5): Add pairwise project comparisons and recover rankings using a Bradley-Terry style estimator or another defensible method. Threat Model (+3): Publish a written threat model covering voting and submission abuse, including attacks such as Sybil voting, ballot stuffing, submission scraping, judge collusion, and deadline gaming. API First (+3): Expose every UI action through a documented API and publish an OpenAPI specification. Maximum bonus: +16 points. One challenge done properly beats four unfinished features. Prizes ₹250000 Total Prize Pool 1st Place - Grand Prize: ₹80000 2nd Place - Runner-Up: ₹50000 3rd Place: ₹35000 4th Place: ₹20000 5th Place: ₹15000 Best Judging Engine: ₹10000 Write Up Quest: 4 winners × ₹10000 = ₹40000 The 1st-place project will be forked, self-hosted, and put into production for Hackathon Raptors events. The winning team keeps ownership of its repository. Hackathon Raptors does not require an assignment, transfer, CLA, or exclusivity agreement. Rules Teams must contain 1-4 members. Solo participation is allowed. All project code must be written during the official 72-hour hackathon window. Planning, research, documentation reading, and AI prompt preparation are allowed before kickoff. No project code may be committed before kickoff. T1 must be completed for the project to be judged. The submitted GitHub repository must be public at submission time. The project must use an OSI-approved open-source license. The project must run locally without hosted-service dependencies. docker compose up must produce a working, seeded portal. The final project must be self-hostable and work without network connectivity. Existing projects cannot be submitted as-is. Renamed copies or rewrites of existing open-source hackathon platforms are not allowed. Tier claims must be honest and supported by the acceptance report. AI coding assistants are allowed. Frameworks, libraries, boilerplate generators, and development tools are allowed. The final software must be something the team can explain and defend. Any project that cannot be run and evaluated as required may not be considered for adoption. Important Dates August 24, 2026: Registration opens. September 4, 2026: Judging panel announced. September 21, 2026: Team formation. September 24, 2026: Full specification published. September 25, 2026 at 18:00 UTC: Hackathon begins. September 28, 2026 at 18:00 UTC: Code freeze and submission deadline. September 28 to October 8, 2026: Judging window. October 5, 2026 at 18:00 UTC: Write Up Quest closes. October 9, 2026: Winners announced. About Hackathon Raptors Hackathon Raptors is a Community Interest Company that runs online hackathons for working engineers and developers. 35+ hackathons run since 2023. Participants from 85+ countries. Roughly a dozen events run each year. 300+ projects have been submitted in our last hackathon. Events are designed around practical engineering challenges rather than purely conceptual ideas. Dogfood is built around one simple proposition: Build the platform that will judge you.
prize: 1st Place: ₹80000 | 2nd Place: ₹50000 | 3rd Place: ₹35000 | 4th Place: ₹20000 | 5th Place: ₹15000 | Best Judging Engine: ₹10000 | Write Up Quest | Side quest $100 x 4: ₹40000

title: Code and Craft - SSN SNUC Invente '26
description: Code and Craft is the premier Design & Development competition, where you can showcase your creativity and subject your development skills to bring it to life. Code it. Craft it. Show it. Guidelines: Eligibility: Open to students from all colleges and universities Team Size: 1-3 participants per team Inter-College Teams: Allowed. Participants from different colleges may form a team Inter-Specialization Teams: Allowed. Participants from differents branches/specializations may form a team. Competition Format: The competition consists of three rounds: Ideate and Create - Design and conceptualization Bring to Life - Website development and implementation Showcase - Live demonstration and Q&A Problem Statements: A theme/problem statement will be provided by the organizers at the beginning of the competition. Teams must develop their solution around the given theme. Design Tools: Participants may use any design tool of their choice; Figma is preferred. Development Tools: Participants may use any suitable technology, including HTML, CSS, JavaScript, frameworks, or approved no-code platforms. Submission: All deliverables must be submitted through the official submission portal within the specified deadline. Presentation: Teams must be prepared to explain their ideation, design process, technology choices, implementation, and final product during the showcase. Rules: General Rules All work must be original and created from scratch. Templates, copied websites, plagiarized designs, and previously completed projects are not permitted. The final solution must clearly address and reflect the given theme/problem statement. Teams must adhere to the specified team size of 1-3 participants. Participants must submit their work within the specified deadline to qualify for the subsequent round. Participants are responsible for ensuring that their project is functional and ready for demonstration during the showcase. Any form of plagiarism or submission of substantially pre-existing work may result in disqualification . Round 1 - Ideate and Create Teams must brainstorm and develop their solution based on the given theme/problem statement. Teams must submit wireframes and/or high-fidelity mockups . AI tools may be used only for ideation and brainstorming . AI must not be used to generate the mockups or design assets. The submitted design must be the team's own work. Round 2 - Bring to Life Teams must develop a working and responsive website based on their submitted design. The website must include at least one meaningful interactive feature , such as an animation, quiz, form, dynamic interaction, or similar functionality. The implementation should maintain consistency with the submitted design. AI tools may be used for website implementation , but the final website must reflect the team's own design decisions. Any technology or development stack may be used, including coding and permitted no-code platforms. Round 3 - Showcase Teams must provide a live demonstration of their final website. Teams must explain: The initial idea and brainstorming process Problem interpretation Wireframes and mockups Design decisions Team members' contributions Technology/stack selection Development process Interactive features Final implementation Judges may question participants about any stage of the competition . Participants should be able to justify their design and technical decisions. Tie-Breaker In case of a tie, design quality, accessibility, usability, and consistency between the submitted design and final implementation will be scrutinized.

Individual and Team participation is allowed. Inter-college teams are allowed. Students from different specializations and colleges can form a team. Each team can select and build one track only . Participants must meet the eligibility criteria individually. Participants from different engineering specializations are allowed to collaborate within the same team. Format Mode: Online Participation: Individual or Team Build Duration: 24 September 2026, 10:00 AM IST to 26 September 2026, 10:00 PM IST Total Build Time: 60 hours There are 6 problem tracks , and each participant must choose one track . Tracks Tracks will be updated soon!!! Submission Requirements Each participant must submit: A runnable project with a deployed link GitHub repository with setup instructions A 3-minute demo video A PPT presentation explaining the project (maximum upto 10 slides) Disclosure of AI tools used The PPT should clearly explain the problem, approach, solution, key features, technology stack, architecture or workflow, results, and demo. Participants are responsible for ensuring that their submissions are original and that external resources, datasets, models, APIs, and AI tools used are appropriately disclosed. Prize selection and internship selection are separate decisions. Up to 10 internship selections will be made following the evaluation and interview process.

title: EVOX 1.0
description: THEME REVEAL: 22nd September Something's Coming... A Prompt Competition Unlike Any Other Get ready for a competition that flips the script on what "prompting" means. You've written prompts to get answers, images, essays, code... but this time, we're taking it a step further. This competition will challenge you to go beyond just writing a prompt - you'll be creating something entirely new with it. Think less "chatbot conversation" and more "building your own working application" - powered entirely by prompts. The theme is still under wraps - but here's a hint: it involves AI, creativity, logic, and a whole lot of imagination. Why you should be excited: A completely new kind of prompt-based challenge - not your typical "write a prompt" competition Build a working app/software using nothing but the power of prompts A chance to explore AI tools in a hands-on, creative way Build something real, something you can showcase No prior technical expertise needed - just curiosity and creativity Who can participate? Open to all students and enthusiasts who want to explore the intersection of AI and creativity. Team Size: 1-4 members per team What to expect: The theme will be revealed on 22nd September You'll use prompts to build and shape your creation Submission opens after the theme reveal, along with rules and guidelines Rewards: E-certificates for all participants Exciting prizes - to be announced soon! Don't miss it: Theme drops 22nd September Here's the reveal description: THE THEME IS HERE! Challenge: Build a Game - Any Concept, Any Type The wait is over. Here's what you'll be creating: Your Task: Design and build a game - any concept, any genre, any style you can imagine. The only requirement: it has to be innovative . Use AI prompting to bring your idea to life from concept to final build. Judging Criteria: Your submission will be evaluated on: Innovation - how original and fresh is your concept? Game Creativity - how imaginative is the gameplay/design? Approach - how well thought-out is your process? Prompting - how effectively did you use prompts to build your game? Engaging Uniqueness - does it stand out and hold attention? Submission Requirements: Live Deployed Link and, You need to submit a single PDF with two things: Page 1: A write-up explaining the concept of your game From the next Page: The exact prompts you used to create your game Team Size: 1-4 members Time to bring your wildest game ideas to life - powered entirely by prompts. Let's see what you build.

Build something that matters. Build for Bharat 2.0 36 Hours. Real Problems. Real Solutions. ₹20.50 Lakhs+ in Rewards.

title: YODHA 2.0 - Warriors of AI | National-Level 48-Hour Hackathon
description: Overview: YODHA 2.0 - Warriors of AI is a National-Level 48-Hour AI Hackathon organized by the Department of Artificial Intelligence and Data Science, Jyothi Engineering College (Autonomous), Cheruthuruthy. Following the successful completion of the first edition, YODHA returns with its second edition, providing a platform for students and innovators to showcase their creativity, technical skills, and problem-solving abilities. Theme: AI for Healthcare Participants will develop innovative and practical AI-driven solutions to address real-world healthcare challenges. During the 48-hour hackathon, teams will collaborate, build prototypes, receive mentoring, and present their solutions before an expert judging panel. Registration & Problem Statements Participants can register through the official YODHA website and explore the available problem statements: https://yodha.aidajecc.in/ YODHA 2.0 is an opportunity for students to learn, collaborate, innovate, and build technology-driven solutions that can create meaningful impact in healthcare. Event Details: Event: YODHA 2.0 - Warriors of AI Date: 1st-3rd October 2026 Duration: 48 Hours Mode: Offline Venue: Jyothi Engineering College (Autonomous), Cheruthuruthy Theme: AI for Healthcare Eligibility: Open to college students from India. Participants should register as a team. Students from different engineering and technology backgrounds can participate. Participants should have an interest in Artificial Intelligence, technology, innovation, and problem-solving. Hackathon Process: Phase 1: Online Registration: Teams register through the official registration platform. Phase 2: Problem Statement Release & Idea Submission: Teams submit their innovative idea based on the provided problem statements. title: WebRush - 6-Hour Frontend Hackathon
description: Overview WebRush - 6-Hour Frontend Hackathon WebRush is a fully online, individual frontend hackathon where participants get 6 hours to build a complete web solution for a given challenge . But there's a twist - you don't get just one shot at your score. The Challenge At the beginning of the hackathon, one common problem statement will be provided to all participants. Your task is to design and develop the best possible frontend solution within the 6-hour time limit . You can choose your own approach, design, frontend framework, libraries, and tools - but your final submission must follow the challenge requirements. Automated Evaluation with FAIE Engine Your project will be evaluated automatically using the FAIE Engine , an automated frontend evaluation and scoring system. The evaluation focuses on aspects such as: UI/UX & Visual Quality Required Features & Functionality Code Quality & Structure Responsiveness Accessibility & Performance Project Documentation Overall implementation of the given challenge No manual judging panel is required for scoring. Your submission is analyzed and scored through the evaluation engine. 3 Chances to Improve Your Score Every participant gets up to 3 chances to submit and improve their project during the allowed submission window. You can use these attempts strategically: Build → Evaluate → Improve → Resubmit Each evaluation provides a score, allowing you to identify areas that need improvement and work towards a better final score. Your highest valid score will be considered for the final leaderboard. Leaderboard = Final Results This isn't just about completing the challenge - your score determines your position. Participants will be ranked on the final leaderboard based on their highest achieved score . Highest Rank → Winner Second Highest Rank → Runner-Up Other top-ranked participants → As per the final leaderboard ️ Technology Rules Individual participation only. Fully online hackathon. Frontend development only. Modern frontend frameworks, libraries, UI tools, and development tools are allowed. Backend technologies and backend implementation are not allowed. The project must be developed within the 6-hour hackathon duration . Previously built projects cannot be submitted. Submission Participants will submit: Live deployed website GitHub repository Required project details All submissions must be made within the specified hackathon timeline. One Challenge. Six Hours. Three Chances. One Leaderboard. Build fast. Get evaluated. Improve your score. Climb the leaderboard. Welcome to WebRush.

title: EIC VentureX: Idea To Impact Hackathon
description: EIC VentureX: Idea to Impact Stop scrolling, start building. Most people have ideas. Very few have the guts to build and pitch them in front of VCs, founders, and industry leaders. EIC VentureX: Idea to Impact is your shot. Organized by the Entrepreneurship & Incubation Cell (EIC), VentureX is a premier startup pitching competition open to students and working professionals across India. This isn't just a hackathon, it's a launchpad. A room full of the right people, the right energy, and the right opportunities to turn your idea into something real. What Makes VentureX Different? Forget participation trophies and hollow certificates. Venture Capitalists will be present at the Grand Finale, and your pitch could literally change your life. Top 3 winning teams get a curated, invite-only networking lunch with founders and co-founders, worth ₹5,000 per team. Top 2 teams get a dedicated opportunity to pitch directly in front of Venture Capitalists, an experience worth ₹10,000, absolutely free for you. Shortlisted finalists also get exclusive access to our E-Summit, where you network with the startup ecosystem, investors, entrepreneurs, mentors, and innovators all under one roof. This is the room you've been trying to get into, and VentureX opens the door. Who Should Apply? VentureX is for you if you have an idea that solves a real problem, want to experience what a real startup pitch feels like, are ready to be challenged by mentors, judges, and VCs, and want to build your network beyond your campus. Open to undergraduate students, postgraduate students, and working professionals across India. Cross-college teams are welcome, and so are cross-city teams. Competition Structure VentureX runs across three stages. Round 1A is a mandatory online Team Quiz lasting 20 minutes, covering entrepreneurship basics, problem-solving aptitude, and general startup thinking. Every team member must participate individually, and no retakes are allowed. Round 1B is the Online Pitching Round, spread over 2 days. Once registrations close, your team can pick a problem that already excites you or take on one of ours, and go from zero to pitch-ready. Teams must submit a 6 to 7 slide Solution Deck covering the problem, your solution, how it works, market opportunity, business model, and your team, with an optional slide for traction or roadmap. A ready-to-use template will be shared with all registered teams. Submissions are accepted as PDF or PPT only, with a max file size of 20 MB. A short 2-4 minute video pitch is optional but recommended, uploaded to YouTube (unlisted) or Google Drive. Round 2 is the Grand Finale, held in person (tentatively) at PEC, Chandigarh. Only the best teams from Round 1 make it here, and this round is not just another pitching round, it's an on-site hackathon where shortlisted teams take their ideas from concept to a functional product. Teams are expected to build a finished MVP that can be demonstrated during the final pitch, functional enough to show the core value proposition and key working aspects of the solution. You're free to use any tools you're comfortable with, including vibe coding, no-code or low-code tools, and AI-powered development tools. The focus isn't on how you write every line of code, it's on whether you can turn your idea into a functional product. Final deliverables include a finished MVP, a PPT pitch deck, a product demonstration, and any supporting material needed to communicate your solution effectively. Round 1: prove it. Round 2: build it. Final Pitch: defend it. VentureX: Idea to Impact.

title: Genie X Hub represents Project : Eclipse Hackathon
description: Genie X Hub Presents: PROJECT ECLIPSE HACKATHON Build AI That Thinks, Acts & Automates - Not Just Answers. Project Eclipse Hackathon is a hybrid AI-focused hackathon by Genie Hive Private Limited , designed for college students, developers, AI enthusiasts, designers, and innovators who want to build practical solutions using Generative AI, Agentic AI, Autonomous Systems, and Intelligent Automation . This is more than a conventional chatbot-building competition. Participants are challenged to build systems that can understand problems, reason, use tools and APIs, execute actions, verify outcomes, and involve humans when necessary . The hackathon features 5 curated real-world AI challenges + 1 Open Innovation challenge . Whatsapp Community: Join this community for all the event updates : https://chat.whatsapp.com/CwOLKlgym1W4TpcNDx8TUC THE ECLIPSE CHALLENGE AI is moving beyond systems that simply generate responses. Project Eclipse focuses on systems that follow the workflow: INPUT → UNDERSTAND → PLAN → USE TOOLS → ACT → VERIFY → RECOVER / ESCALATE Participants are encouraged to build working AI systems that solve meaningful problems and demonstrate real task completion rather than simply generating convincing text. CHALLENGE TRACKS Participants can choose one of five curated challenges or participate in the OPEN-X Open Innovation Challenge . 01 - AI Agent for Production Incident Investigation & Recovery Build an autonomous production-operations agent that investigates a simulated production incident across application logs, infrastructure metrics, deployment history, Git commits, alerts, and service dependencies. The system should demonstrate capabilities such as: • Multi-source investigation • Tool/API calling • Reasoning over temporal events • Root-cause hypothesis generation • Confidence estimation • Remediation planning • Human approval for high-impact actions • Recovery verification • Post-incident report generation 02 - Autonomous Resolution of Cross-System Transaction Mismatches Build an AI agent that investigates transaction mismatches across invoices, payment records, purchase orders, emails, spreadsheets, and accounting/ERP systems. The system should be able to: • Ingest data from multiple sources • Match transactions/entities • Retrieve supporting evidence • Classify discrepancies using context • Detect partial, duplicate, or missing payments • Recommend appropriate actions • Maintain an auditable action trail • Use human approval for consequential updates 03 - From Contract Language to Executable Business Actions Build an AI agent that converts contracts into executable compliance workflows. Your system should be able to: • Extract obligations • Identify responsible parties and deadlines • Reason over conditional clauses • Generate tasks and workflows • Send reminders and escalations • Maintain compliance records • Handle document hierarchy and amendments • Resolve conflicts between contract documents and instructions 04 - Autonomous Requirement-to-Quotation Procurement System Build an AI procurement agent that takes a natural-language purchase requirement and analyzes vendor quotations. The system should: • Understand requirements • Parse quotations from documents, emails, or structured files • Normalize specifications • Check mandatory constraints • Compare cost and trade-offs • Detect anomalies • Simulate vendor clarification/negotiation • Prepare a recommendation for human approval The goal is not simply to identify the cheapest quotation, but to determine whether a quotation actually satisfies the required specifications. 05 - Issue-to-Pull-Request AI Engineering Agent Build an AI software-engineering agent that receives a repository, issue description, and acceptance criteria and takes the problem from: ISSUE → INVESTIGATION → IMPLEMENTATION → TESTING → PULL REQUEST The agent should demonstrate: • Repository exploration • Issue and acceptance-criteria understanding • Technical hypothesis formation • Code modification • Test execution • Failure analysis and iteration • Patch/PR generation • Human review before deployment OPEN-X - OPEN INNOVATION Have your own problem worth solving? Build beyond the brief. In OPEN-X , participants can define their own real-world problem and build an original solution using Generative AI, Agentic AI, Autonomous Workflows, or Intelligent Automation . Your submission should explain: Problem - What real-world problem are you solving? Target Users - Who experiences this problem? Existing Gap - Why are existing approaches insufficient? Proposed Solution - What are you building and how does it work? AI / Agent Component - Why does the solution meaningfully require GenAI, agents, or intelligent automation? Demonstration - Can you demonstrate the system working end-to-end? Impact - What changes if your solution is deployed? A conventional application with an AI label added on top is not sufficient for the Open Innovation challenge. ️ HACKATHON TIMELINE Registration 20 September - 30 September 2026 Online Round 1 - Idea Submission 01 October - 06 October 2026 Online Shortlisted Teams Announcement 09 October 2026 Round 2 - Building Phase 11 October - 23 October 2026 Online Finalists Announcement 25 October 2026 Grand Finale 27 October 2026 Offline - Chennai, Tamil Nadu, India Grand Finale venue: To Be Announced All preliminary rounds will be conducted online. The Grand Finale will be conducted offline in Chennai. Whatsapp Community: Join this community for all the event updates : https://chat.whatsapp.com/CwOLKlgym1W4TpcNDx8TUC ROUND 2 PARTICIPATION FEE ₹499 INR Initial registration and Round 1 participation are FREE. Only teams that are shortlisted for Round 2 will be required to pay the ₹499 INR Round 2 participation fee to enter the building phase. The fee is not applicable during initial registration or Round 1 . Participation flow: Register → FREE Round 1 Idea Submission → FREE Shortlisted for Round 2 → ₹499 Round 2 Building Phase → Build & Submit Selected as Finalist → Grand Finale ️ HOW THE HACKATHON WORKS ROUND 1 - IDEA SUBMISSION Participants select one of the five curated challenges or choose the OPEN-X track. Teams submit their proposed solution, explaining the problem, approach, AI/agent architecture, workflow, and expected impact. Submissions will be evaluated based on problem relevance, proposed approach, technical potential, use of AI/agentic systems, and overall solution quality. Shortlisted teams will advance to Round 2. ROUND 2 - BUILD Shortlisted teams will transform their ideas into a functional and demonstrable prototype . Participants should aim to demonstrate an end-to-end system rather than a concept or basic chatbot. For agentic solutions, the recommended execution flow is: INPUT → PLAN → TOOL USE → DECISION → ACTION → VERIFICATION Systems should demonstrate meaningful task completion, reliability, and appropriate handling of failures or situations requiring human intervention. GRAND FINALE Finalists will present their working solutions to the judging panel at the offline Grand Finale in Chennai, Tamil Nadu . Final presentations will focus on: • Working product demonstration • Technical implementation • Agentic reasoning • Tool/API integration • Autonomous execution • Reliability and failure handling • Innovation • User experience • Real-world applicability JUDGING CRITERIA Criterion Weight Problem Understanding & Relevance 10% Agentic Reasoning & Planning 20% Tool / API / System Integration 15% Autonomous Task Completion 20% Reliability & Failure Handling 15% Innovation 10% UX / Demonstration 10% Total 100% These criteria are based on the official challenge framework for the hackathon. SUBMISSION EXPECTATIONS Participants should prepare a working prototype or demonstrable implementation . Depending on the selected challenge, submissions may include: • Working prototype • Problem and solution explanation • Architecture/workflow diagram • AI/agent architecture • Tools and APIs used • Repository/code submission where required • Demo video or live demonstration • Known limitations • Safety controls • Future scope For agentic submissions, participants are encouraged to make the execution trace visible: INPUT → PLAN → TOOL USE → DECISION → ACTION → VERIFICATION WHO CAN PARTICIPATE? Project Eclipse Hackathon is open to college and university students. Participants interested in the following areas are encouraged to participate: • Generative AI • Agentic AI • AI Automation • Machine Learning • Software Engineering • Data & Analytics • Developer Tools • Enterprise Automation • Product Development • Emerging Technologies You don't need to be an AI expert. If you can identify a meaningful problem and build a solution around it, Project Eclipse is for you. ️ TECHNOLOGIES Participants may use appropriate technologies, frameworks, APIs, cloud services, open-source models, datasets, and development tools, subject to the final hackathon rules and applicable usage limits. PS-03: AI-Based Waste Segregation Build an intelligent system capable of identifying different categories of waste using computer vision and automatically assisting in segregation at the point of disposal. PS-04: Smart Retail Shelf Monitoring Develop an edge-AI solution that detects empty shelves, misplaced products, and inventory conditions using cameras and provides real-time notifications. Track 2: Healthcare & Assistive Technology PS-05: AI-Powered Assistive System for Visually Impaired People Develop a portable intelligent device that uses computer vision and on-device AI to identify obstacles, objects, signs, or people and communicate useful information through audio or haptic feedback. PS-06: Edge AI-Based Elderly Fall Detection Develop a privacy-preserving system that detects when an elderly person falls and automatically generates an emergency alert without requiring continuous cloud processing. PS-07: Intelligent Stress & Wellness Monitor Develop an edge-AI system that analyzes physiological or behavioral signals to estimate stress/wellness levels in real time and provide personalized recommendations. PS-08: Smart Medicine Management System Develop an intelligent connected device that helps users manage medication schedules, detects missed doses, and provides alerts to caregivers when necessary. Track 3: Smart City & Sustainability PS-09: Intelligent Traffic Management Develop an edge-AI system that analyzes traffic conditions in real time and dynamically recommends signal timing or traffic-routing strategies to reduce congestion. PS-10: Smart Energy Optimization Build an IoT and Edge AI solution that monitors electricity consumption and intelligently recommends or automatically implements energy-saving actions. PS-11: AI-Based Water Leakage Detection Develop a sensor-based intelligent system that detects abnormal water flow or leakage and generates real-time alerts to minimize water wastage. PS-12: Smart Air Quality Monitoring Develop a low-cost connected device that monitors environmental parameters and uses edge intelligence to identify pollution patterns and provide actionable alerts. Track 4: Smart Mobility & Robotics PS-13: Intelligent Autonomous Delivery Robot Design a small autonomous robot capable of navigating a defined environment, avoiding obstacles, identifying its destination, and safely delivering objects. PS-14: AI-Based Driver Assistance System Develop an edge-AI solution capable of detecting driver distraction, drowsiness, lane departure, or nearby obstacles and generating timely warnings. PS-15: Smart Agricultural Rover Develop an autonomous agricultural robot that can monitor crops, identify plant health conditions, detect weeds, or assist with precision agriculture. PS-16: Search-and-Rescue Intelligent Robot Develop a robotic system capable of navigating hazardous or difficult environments while detecting people, obstacles, temperature anomalies, or other indicators useful during rescue operations. Track 5: Connected Intelligence & IoT PS-17: Smart Home Energy Guardian Develop an intelligent IoT system that monitors household appliances and automatically identifies unnecessary energy consumption and abnormal usage patterns. PS-18: Intelligent Industrial Monitoring System Develop an edge-IoT solution that monitors machines using sensors and detects abnormal operating conditions before equipment failure occurs. PS-19: Smart Agriculture Monitoring Platform Build an IoT system that monitors soil moisture, temperature, humidity, and other agricultural parameters & uses AI to recommend irrigation or crop-management actions. PS-20: Connected Disaster Alert System Develop a resilient IoT-based system capable of detecting conditions such as floods, fires, earthquakes, or other environmental hazards and distributing local emergency alerts even when conventional connectivity is limited

title: Singularity Hackathon
organizer: AJ Institute of Engineering and Technology (AJIET), Mangalore, Karnataka
description: Overview The Singularity is a National-Level Artificial Intelligence Hackathon that is a software-focused competition designed to provide students with an opportunity to demonstrate their technical expertise, problem-solving abilities, innovation, and software development skills in the field of Artificial Intelligence . The hackathon will be conducted in two rounds . The first round will involve profile-based screening of registered teams. Shortlisted teams will advance to the offline final round, where they will be presented with AI-focused problem statements revealed during the event. Eligibility The hackathon is open to students from colleges and educational institutions across India. All participants must register through Unstop . Each team must consist of a minimum of 2 and a maximum of 4 members . Inter-college teams are permitted. Inter-branch and inter-specialization teams are permitted. Team members may belong to different academic disciplines, branches, or specializations. Each participant may register as a member of only one team . All participants must provide accurate and valid information during registration. Shortlisted teams must comply with all requirements and instructions communicated by the organizing committee. Theme and Format Theme: Artificial Intelligence Format: Software Hackathon Hardware: The hackathon is strictly software-based; hardware-based solutions are not required. Tracks The final round will cover the following AI-focused domains: AI for Coastal Intelligence AI for Supply Chain Intelligence AI for Industrial Intelligence Teams will be presented with a specific problem statement within one of these domains at the beginning of the offline hackathon . Teams will be required to design, develop, and demonstrate a functional software solution within the specified hackathon duration. Registration and Participation Fee Round 1 Registration Fee: Free Round 2 Final Round Fee: ₹650 per shortlisted team The ₹650 fee is applicable per team and not per participant . The final-round participation fee includes: Accommodation during the hackathon Food during the event Travel expenses are not included and must be borne by the participants. Registration and official communication regarding the hackathon will be conducted through Unstop and the official communication channels of the organizing committee. Team Rules Each team must consist of a minimum of 2 and a maximum of 4 members . Inter-college teams are allowed. Inter-branch and inter-specialization teams are allowed. A participant cannot be a member of more than one team . All team members must provide accurate and verifiable information. Any change in team composition after shortlisting requires prior approval from the organizing committee . Only shortlisted teams that complete the required final-round registration process will be eligible to participate in the offline hackathon. All team members must report to the designated venue within the specified reporting time. Participants must carry a valid college/student identification document for verification. Participants are responsible for making their own travel arrangements and covering their travel expenses. Teams must comply with all instructions and guidelines issued by the organizing committee. Hackathon Rules The hackathon is strictly software-based and focuses on the theme of Artificial Intelligence . Hardware-based submissions are not permitted under any circumstances. Problem statements or tracks will be disclosed at the beginning of the offline round . Teams must develop their solutions within the specified hackathon duration . Each team must submit and demonstrate its own solution . Plagiarism, impersonation, unauthorized copying, or submission of another team's work will result in immediate disqualification. Teams may use existing libraries, frameworks, APIs, open-source tools, and publicly available resources, subject to the guidelines provided during the event. Previously developed projects must not be submitted as a complete solution to the assigned problem statement. Any external datasets, APIs, models, libraries, or other resources used in a project must be appropriately acknowledged wherever required. Teams must ensure that their submissions comply with applicable intellectual property, licensing, and usage requirements. Any attempt to manipulate the evaluation process, misrepresent information, or violate the hackathon rules may result in disqualification . Participants must maintain professional conduct and follow the instructions of the organizing committee, mentors, and judges throughout the event. The decision of the judging panel and organizing committee will be final and binding . The organizing committee reserves the right to modify the schedule, rules, format, or other event-related details if circumstances require. Any significant changes will be communicated through the official communication channels. By registering for and participating in the National-Level Artificial Intelligence Hackathon , all participants acknowledge and agree to comply with the rules, guidelines, requirements, and decisions of the organizing committee and judging panel.

title: HACK ON TRACK (24-Hour National Hackathon)
organizer: FR. C. Rodrigues Institute of Technology (FCRIT), Navi Mumbai
description: Team Size: 1-4 members. Teams must be finalized before the event; no switching mid-hackathon. Format - 3 Rounds: Round 1: PPT Submission (₹250 registration): Each team selects a domain and submits an abstract/PPT solution for it. Submissions are evaluated on innovation, feasibility, and relevance. Shortlisted teams advance to the offline hackathon and their selected domain carries forward to Round 2. Round 2: 24-Hour Offline Hackathon 8th-9th October 2026 | FCRIT, Vashi Your domain from Round 1 stays fixed it does not change. At check-in, each team picks a color, which maps to one of three options within your domain: Problem Statement 1 , Problem Statement 2 , or Open Innovation . The mapping is revealed at the Inauguration Ceremony. Teams assigned a predefined problem statement must work on it as is no switching. Teams assigned Open Innovation have the flexibility to either stay with Open Innovation or switch to one of the two predefined problem statements in their domain, if they prefer more structure. This keeps the process fair everyone works within the expertise they've already committed to, the exact challenge stays a surprise until the event starts, and teams that land on Open Innovation aren't locked out of a more defined problem if they'd rather have one. Teams build and submit progress through scheduled Git check-ins, with mentoring support throughout. The top 10 teams from Round 2 advance to the final. Round 3: Final Evaluation: Top 10 teams present before the jury: 7-minute presentation, 3-minute Q&A. A live working prototype demonstration is mandatory. What You Need to Build: Address a clear, meaningful real-world problem Demonstrate solid technical implementation Showcase practical thinking and innovation Be explainable and demonstrable by the team Prizes: Cash prizes and exclusive goodies for winning teams. Certificates of participation for all, and certificates of excellence for top performers. Build. Innovate. Compete: Get ready for 24 hours of problem-solving, technology, teamwork, and innovation.

title: Zephyr CTF 2026
organizer: Thakur College Of Engineering And Technology
description: Event Details: Date: 30 September 2026 Time: 10 AM - 5 PM Mode: On-campus Venue: Thakur College of Engineering and Technology (TCET), Mumbai Team Size: 1-2 Participants Format: Jeopardy-style Capture the Flag Domains Covered: Participants will encounter challenges across multiple areas of cybersecurity, including: Web Exploitation Cryptography Digital Forensics Open-Source Intelligence (OSINT) Reverse Engineering Linux & System Security Miscellaneous Stegnography AI/ML Each category is designed to test a different aspect of cybersecurity knowledge. Participants may need to investigate clues, analyze files, exploit vulnerabilities, decode information, inspect applications, and think beyond the obvious to uncover the correct flags. Eligibility: ZEPHYR CTF 2026 is open to students and cybersecurity enthusiasts interested in exploring practical cybersecurity through Capture the Flag challenges. The competition welcomes: Cybersecurity enthusiasts College students Beginners interested in cybersecurity Programmers and developers Ethical hacking enthusiasts Students from technical and interdisciplinary backgrounds Participants do not need extensive prior CTF experience to participate. Familiarity with basic cybersecurity concepts, Linux, networking, or programming can be helpful. Teams may consist of one to two members , and participants may form teams across different colleges, subject to the event's registration requirements. Competition Format: ZEPHYR follows a Jeopardy-style CTF format hosted on a dedicated CTFd platform . Participants will have access to challenges across different categories and can choose which challenges to attempt. Successfully solving a challenge and submitting the correct flag awards points to the team. A live leaderboard will track participant progress throughout the competition. The team accumulating the highest score at the end of the competition will be determined according to the official scoring and tie-breaking rules. Why Participate? ZEPHYR CTF gives participants an opportunity to: Apply cybersecurity concepts to practical challenges Develop problem-solving and analytical skills Explore different domains of cybersecurity Gain hands-on Capture the Flag experience Work collaboratively under time pressure Test their technical knowledge in a competitive environment Discover areas of cybersecurity they may want to explore further Whether you are attempting your first CTF or already have experience solving security challenges, ZEPHYR provides a platform to learn, experiment, compete, and challenge yourself . Rules and Code of Conduct: Participants are expected to maintain fair play and professionalism throughout the competition. Attacking or attempting to disrupt the CTF infrastructure is strictly prohibited. DDoS attacks, destructive actions, or infrastructure abuse are prohibited. Sharing flags, solutions, or challenge answers between teams is not permitted. Use of AI is permitted Participants must ensure that their submissions comply with the stated AI usage guidelines & be able to clearly explain their approach, reasoning, and how they arrived at their solutions. Participants must not attack or interfere with other participants. Challenges must be solved within the environments and scope provided by the organizers. Plagiarism, impersonation, or other forms of unfair practice may result in disqualification. Any attempt to compromise the integrity or availability of the competition infrastructure may result in immediate disqualification. Participants are responsible for bringing a functional laptop and any required personal equipment. The organizers reserve the right to take appropriate action in case of rule violations or disputes. What to Bring: Participants are advised to bring: A personal laptop Laptop charger Stable internet access / mobile hotspot as a backup A modern web browser Any personal cybersecurity tools they normally use for CTFs Flag Format: Flags will follow the designated format: OWASP_TCET{...} Participants should submit discovered flags through the official CTFd platform .

title: Narayana National Hackathon 2026
organizer: Jai Narayan Vidya Mandir, Kanpur, Uttar Pradesh
description: Narayana National Hackathon 2026 is a multi-stage technology and innovation hackathon organized by Jai Narayan Vidya Mandir, Uttar Pradesh , to provide students, developers, innovators, and emerging technologists with a platform to identify real-world problems, develop technology-driven solutions, build functional prototypes, and present their innovations before an evaluation panel. The hackathon is designed as a 5-round competitive innovation journey , beginning with registration and idea submission and progressing through idea evaluation, prototype development, technical evaluation, and finally the Grand Finale . Participants will have the opportunity to work on innovative solutions across domains such as Artificial Intelligence & Machine Learning, Web Development, Mobile Applications, Cloud Computing, Data Science, Cybersecurity, Blockchain, IoT, Automation, SaaS, and other emerging technologies , depending on the selected problem statement or theme. The objective is not simply to develop an idea, but to transform that idea into a practical, technically feasible, scalable, and impactful solution . Registration: Registration Fee: FREE Registration for Narayana National Hackathon 2026 is completely free of cost . Participants are not required to pay any registration fee or participation fee to register for the hackathon. Why Participate? Narayana National Hackathon 2026 provides participants with an opportunity to: Solve real-world and technology-driven problems. Convert innovative ideas into functional prototypes. Work with modern technologies and development frameworks. Demonstrate technical and problem-solving skills. Gain experience in product development and innovation. Present their solutions before an evaluation panel. Compete with teams from different colleges and institutions. Receive recognition for their innovation and technical contribution. Build a project that can potentially be developed further beyond the hackathon. Experience the complete journey from Idea → Validation → Development → Evaluation → Final Presentation . Compete for a total prize pool of ₹1,00,000 . Hackathon Format The competition will be conducted through 5 rounds . Round 1: Registration & Idea Submission Participants will register for the hackathon and form their teams according to the participation guidelines. After registration, teams will select a suitable problem statement/theme and submit their initial idea. The submission may include: Team details Problem statement/title Problem identification Proposed solution Key features Target users Expected impact Proposed technology stack Initial implementation approach The purpose of this round is to understand the problem being addressed and the innovation proposed by the team . Teams should clearly explain what problem they are trying to solve and how their proposed technology-based solution can address it. Round 2: Idea Evaluation & Shortlisting All submitted ideas will go through an evaluation process. The evaluation may consider: Understanding of the problem Relevance of the proposed solution Innovation and originality Technical feasibility Practical applicability Scalability Potential impact Clarity of the proposed approach Based on the evaluation, selected teams will move to the prototype development stage. Teams qualifying for the next stage will receive further instructions regarding the development and submission requirements. Round 3: Prototype Development This round focuses on converting the selected idea into a working prototype or Minimum Viable Product (MVP) . Teams will be expected to develop a demonstrable version of their proposed solution. Depending on the selected problem statement, the prototype may include: Web application Mobile application AI/ML solution SaaS platform Cloud-based application Data-driven solution Automation system IoT-based solution Blockchain-based solution Cybersecurity solution Developer tool Digital platform Other technology-driven solutions Open Innovation Teams should demonstrate the actual functionality of their solution rather than presenting only a conceptual idea. Prototype Submission Teams may be required to provide: Project description Functional prototype/MVP Source code/repository, where applicable Presentation/PPT Architecture diagram Technology stack Feature explanation Demo video Live deployment/prototype link, wherever applicable Additional supporting information The project submission structure will focus on the proposed solution, architecture, innovation, technical details, existing-solution comparison, demonstration, and live deployment/prototype wherever applicable. Round 4: Technical Evaluation & Project Demonstration Shortlisted teams will proceed to the technical evaluation stage. Teams will demonstrate their developed prototype and explain how their solution addresses the selected problem. The evaluation panel may consider: Problem Understanding How clearly does the team understand the problem? Innovation How innovative or differentiated is the proposed solution? Technical Implementation How effectively have the selected technologies been implemented? Functionality Does the prototype work as intended? User Experience Is the solution understandable, usable, and accessible to its intended users? Scalability Can the solution potentially support a larger number of users or expanded use cases? Feasibility Can the solution realistically be implemented beyond the hackathon? Impact What potential value can the solution create? Presentation How clearly does the team communicate its idea, architecture, implementation, and future scope? Demonstration How effectively does the team demonstrate its working prototype? Round 5: Grand Finale The Grand Finale will be the final stage of Narayana National Hackathon 2026. Top 20 Teams A total of 20 teams will be selected for the Grand Finale based on their performance throughout the preceding rounds. These 20 finalist teams will receive instructions regarding: Final presentation Prototype demonstration Presentation format Schedule Participation mode Technical requirements Grand Finale process Hybrid Grand Finale - Offline + Online To make the Grand Finale accessible to participants from different locations, Narayana National Hackathon 2026 will provide a hybrid participation option. The Grand Finale will support both: Offline Participation Teams who are able and willing to travel to the designated Grand Finale venue can participate physically at the venue . Offline finalists will be able to: Present their solution in person. Demonstrate their prototype before the evaluation panel. Interact with judges and organizers. Interact with other finalist teams. Participate in the on-ground Grand Finale experience. Online Participation Teams that are unable to attend the physical Grand Finale due to: Travel constraints Distance from the venue Location-related limitations Academic commitments Other genuine circumstances will have the option to participate in the Grand Finale online . Online finalists will receive the necessary instructions for: Virtual presentation Online prototype demonstration Video conferencing Screen sharing Technical setup Final evaluation Important Grand Finale Policy The Grand Finale is not restricted exclusively to teams that can travel to the physical venue. All 20 selected finalist teams will have the option of participating through the applicable offline or online mode , subject to the final instructions and technical arrangements communicated by the organizers. The hybrid format is intended to provide finalists with flexibility and ensure that travel or geographical limitations do not prevent a selected team from presenting its innovation . Prize Pool Total Prize Pool: ₹1,00,000 The Narayana National Hackathon 2026 will offer a total prize pool of ₹1,00,000 across multiple award categories. Award Prize Prize Money Winner ₹30,000 First Runner-Up ₹20,000 Second Runner-Up ₹20,000 Best Prototype Project ₹10,000 Best Women Team - Idea Award 1 ₹10,000 Best Women Team - Idea Award 2 ₹10,000 Total Prize Pool ₹1,00,000 Winner The team selected as the overall Winner of Narayana National Hackathon 2026 will receive a prize of: ₹30,000 First Runner-Up The team selected as the First Runner-Up will receive: ₹20,000 Second Runner-Up The team selected as the Second Runner-Up will receive: ₹20,000 Best Prototype Project A special award will be presented to the team demonstrating an outstanding functional prototype/project , with a prize of: ₹10,000 This category recognizes strong prototype development, implementation, functionality, and demonstration. Best Women Team - Idea Awards Two teams will be recognized under the Best Women Team Idea category. Best Women Team Idea - Award 1: ₹10,000 Best Women Team Idea - Award 2: ₹10,000 Total Women Team Idea Awards: ₹20,000 These awards are intended to recognize innovative ideas presented by eligible women-led teams, subject to the eligibility and evaluation criteria communicated by the organizers. Grand Finale Presentation During the Grand Finale, each finalist team will present its solution before the evaluation panel. Teams should be prepared to explain: Problem Statement Problem Background Proposed Solution Target Users Key Features Innovation Technical Architecture Technology Stack Development Approach Working Prototype Live Demonstration Existing Solutions and Comparison Advantages of the Proposed Solution Scalability Future Scope Expected Impact The presentation material should clearly communicate the solution, architecture, innovation, technical implementation, existing-solution comparison, demonstration, and live deployment/prototype wherever applicable. Suggested Technology Domains Participants can build solutions using one or more relevant technology domains, depending on the selected problem statement. Artificial Intelligence & Machine Learning Machine Learning Deep Learning Natural Language Processing Computer Vision Generative AI Recommendation Systems Predictive Analytics Software Development Web Applications Mobile Applications SaaS Platforms Enterprise Applications Developer Tools Automation Systems Cloud & DevOps Cloud Computing Serverless Architecture Containerization APIs Distributed Systems DevOps Data & Analytics Data Science Data Analytics Business Intelligence Predictive Modeling Data Visualization Emerging Technologies Blockchain Internet of Things Cybersecurity Robotics AR/VR Automation Participants are encouraged to choose technologies that are appropriate to the problem rather than using technology merely for complexity . Evaluation Framework Projects may be evaluated across the following dimensions: Evaluation Area What Will Be Considered Problem Understanding Clarity and relevance of the identified problem Innovation Originality and uniqueness of the solution Technical Approach Appropriateness and implementation of technology Functionality Working capability of the prototype Feasibility Practical possibility of implementation Scalability Potential for expansion and larger adoption User Experience Usability and accessibility Impact Potential value and real-world applicability Presentation Clarity and quality of explanation Demonstration Effectiveness of prototype demonstration The exact criteria, weightage, submission requirements, and timelines may be communicated by the organizers for each round. Team Formation Participants may form teams according to the team-size requirements specified by the organizers on the official hackathon opportunity page. Teams are encouraged to have members with complementary skills such as: Frontend Development Backend Development AI/ML Mobile Development UI/UX Database Management Cloud & DevOps Cybersecurity Research Product Development Business/Market Analysis Presentation A multidisciplinary team can help address different aspects of product development, from technical implementation to user experience and presentation. Who Can Participate? The hackathon is intended for students and emerging technology enthusiasts interested in: Software Development Artificial Intelligence Machine Learning Data Science Cloud Computing Web Development Mobile Development Cybersecurity Blockchain IoT Automation Product Development Technology Innovation Participants should review the eligibility and team-size requirements specified on the official hackathon opportunity page before registering. Code of Conduct & Originality All participating teams are expected to maintain professional conduct throughout the hackathon. Participants must: Submit their own work or work they are legally authorized to use. Respect intellectual property rights. Avoid plagiarism. Provide accurate information regarding their project. Disclose the use of third-party APIs, libraries, datasets, open-source components, or external services wherever required. Follow all rules and instructions communicated by the organizers. Any submission found to violate applicable rules may be subject to review or disqualification according to the event guidelines. Prototype & Project Requirements Participants are encouraged to focus on developing a functional and demonstrable solution . The project should clearly communicate: Problem → Solution → Technology → Implementation → Impact Teams should avoid limiting their submission to only: Static PPTs Concept-only proposals Non-functional mockups A functional prototype/MVP is strongly encouraged wherever the selected problem permits it.

title: The Black-Box Protocol: Stage 02 - System Matrix
description: Overview: 12-Hour Offline AI Hack Day in Indore About the Event: Most hackathons end the exact same way: you spend the weekend writing code, show a slide deck, and after the event, the project is abandoned and forgotten. We are here to change that. Organised by TECHhelp4U and backed by Major League Hacking (MLH), with Google Gemini as the official technology partner, Stage 02 // System Matrix is an action-packed, 12-hour offline building sprint in Indore. This isn't just a competition to win prizes-it's a launchpad for your next venture. We want builders to step in with a founder mindset: pick a real problem, build a working AI product using code, and show a clear future roadmap for how you plan to turn your build into a real startup. Top-performing teams will earn direct mentorship, ecosystem support, and fast-track invitations to Stage 03 (Kurukshetra) to help turn their prototypes into active companies! Quick Highlights: Venue: Indore, Madhya Pradesh (in-person offline venue) Duration: 12-hour continuous offline sprint Team Size: 2-4 members Focus Area: 100% Artificial Intelligence (AI) powered by Google Gemini Official Backing: Supported by Major League Hacking (MLH) Perks: Exciting prizes for top podiums, plus assured swag kits, stickers, and goodies for every single participant! What Should You Build? (100% AI Tracks): Stage 02 is exclusively focused on artificial intelligence. We encourage teams to leverage Google Gemini to build intelligent, practical solutions across any of the following focus areas: The Google Gemini Spotlight Track: Build smart applications utilising Google Gemini's multimodal and large-context capabilities: Multimodal Problem Solvers: Applications that process text, audio, images, and video together to solve real-world problems. Deep Context Engines: Tools that analyse large repositories, documents, or knowledge bases in seconds. Context-Aware Assistants: Helpful AI companions that understand user context and automate daily workflows. Autonomous Agents & Workflows: Self-operating task agents that can plan, execute, and troubleshoot without manual oversight. Autonomous research, document synthesis, or customer support workflows. Intelligent bots that assist software teams with code review, automated testing, or bug detection. Developer & Creator Productivity Tools: Smart developer tools, CLI utilities, and automated debugging assistants. Workflow enhancers for writers, creators, designers, or product teams. AI for Real-World Industry Impact: Healthcare & Wellness: AI tools that help organise clinic notes, assist patients, or streamline records. Education & Learning: Personalised interactive tutors and regional language learning tools. Commerce & Small Businesses: Automated bookkeeping, smart support assistants, or intelligent fraud detection. Competition Rounds & Structure: Round 1: Online Application & Idea Screening (Online): Register your team of 2-4 members on Unstop. Submit a brief summary of the problem you want to solve, your planned AI architecture, and your team's background. Shortlisted teams will receive official invitations and an entry badge for the offline finale in Indore. Round 2: The 12-Hour Offline Hack Sprint (Indore): Kickoff & Mentor Sync: Arrive at the venue, set up your workstation, and review your architecture with industry mentors. Build Sprint: 12 hours of uninterrupted coding, debugging, and product development. Live Demonstrations: Present your working project live to the jury and walk through your startup roadmap. Awards & Goodies: Celebrate winning teams, collect your certificates and swag kits, and receive Stage 03 invitations! Eligibility Criteria: Open to all engineering, design, and management students from any college or university across India. Working developers, early-stage founders, and independent builders are warmly welcome. Cross-college and cross-specialisation teams are fully allowed and encouraged. Team size must strictly be between 2 and 4 members. What Do You Need to Submit? Before the 12 hours run out, every team must submit three things: GitHub Repository: A public repository showing active commits made during the event. Live Product Demo: A working application running live. No video recordings or static Figma screens are allowed during judging. Startup Roadmap (1-Page Summary or Short Slide Deck): Target Customer: Who has this problem, and why will they use your solution? Business Model: How will this product sustain itself or generate revenue? Future Milestones: What are the next 3 to 6 steps you will take over the next 3 to 6 months to launch this? How Will You Be Judged? Working Prototype & Live Demo - 30%: Does the software actually function in real time? Is it responsive, usable, and stable? AI Integration & Tech Depth - 30%: How effectively is AI, including Google Gemini, integrated into the core product logic? Is the code clean and well-structured? Problem-Solution Fit & Startup Value - 20%: Does the project solve a real, painful problem that people or businesses would pay for? Future Startup Roadmap - 20%: Does the team have a realistic 3-to-6-month post-hackathon plan to scale this into an active venture? Perks, Rewards & What's In It For You: Exciting Prizes: Prestigious awards for top podium teams and track champions. Assured Swag for Everyone: Exclusive event T-shirts, badge kits, stickers, and official MLH season badges for every single participant. Food & Refreshments: Free meals, coffee, snacks, and energy drinks throughout the 12 hours. Direct Mentorship: One-on-one architectural guidance from experienced AI engineers and founders. Incubation Pathway: Fast-tracked selection into Stage 03 (Kurukshetra) with continuous guidance to help launch your startup. Official Certificates: Verified certificates of participation and excellence backed by TECHhelp4U and partner networks. Code of Conduct & Guidelines: All participants must adhere strictly to the MLH Code of Conduct. Plagiarism, pre-built applications, or submitting projects built before the hackathon start time will lead to immediate disqualification. Respect your peers, mentors, and venue staff at all times. Let's stop building disposable hackathon demos and start building real AI startups!

title: Parallax 2026 - Reality, Reimagined
organizer: Noida Institute of Engineering And Technology (NIET), Greater Noida
