title: Cerebro Hackathon
description: CEREBRO - Neural Sentiment Hackathon Where minds decode emotion at machine speed. CEREBRO is a 36-hour online hackathon organized by the Department of Computer Science & Engineering, Institute of Engineering & Management (IEM), Kolkata . The hackathon challenges participants to build systems that can understand and analyze human emotion, sentiment, and tone across different forms of communication. Participants will choose one of three problem statements and develop a functional solution using their own technology stack, models, and approach. CEREBRO focuses on practical applications of Artificial Intelligence, Machine Learning, Natural Language Processing, Speech Processing, and Affective Computing . Problem Statements PS-01 - Tone Intelligence in Conversations First Prize: ₹5,000 Chat conversations contain more than words. They can reveal tension, sarcasm, warmth, frustration, and escalation. Build a system that analyzes the emotional arc of a multi-turn conversation and identifies changes in tone throughout the conversation. Key requirements: Multi-turn chat sentiment and tone tracking Sarcasm, passive-aggression, and irony detection Emotion-arc visualization over the conversation Support for chat formats such as WhatsApp, Slack, Discord, or similar exports Participants must source their own data and develop their own approach PS-02 - Voice as a Mood Signal Second Prize: ₹3,000 The emotional state behind a sentence can change dramatically depending on how it is spoken. Build a system that extracts emotional information directly from raw audio , using characteristics such as pitch, prosody, speech rate, and pauses. Key requirements: Audio-based emotion classification Continuous valence and arousal estimation Robustness to noisy, accented, or code-switched speech Emotion should primarily be inferred from the audio signal itself Participants must source their own training data PS-03 - Sentiment Drift in Social Threads Third Prize: ₹2,000 Online discussions can begin calmly and quickly become hostile or toxic. Build a system that analyzes a sequence of comments and identifies where the emotional tone changes , including the specific point where sentiment significantly deteriorates. Key requirements: Sequential or graph-based thread modelling Sentiment drift detection Early-warning toxicity signals Data sourced from platforms such as Reddit, X, or YouTube Interpretable output showing which reply contributed to the sentiment shift Prize Pool Total Prize Pool: ₹10,000 Problem Statement Prize PS-01 - Tone Intelligence in Conversations ₹5,000 PS-02 - Voice as a Mood Signal ₹3,000 PS-03 - Sentiment Drift in Social Threads ₹2,000 Total ₹10,000 Schedule Date & Time Event October 15, 2026 Registration opens on Unstop November 1, 2026 Problem statements published November 2, 2026 - 9:00 PM IST Hackathon begins November 3, 2026 - 9:00 AM IST Halfway mark and optional mentor Q&A November 4, 2026 - 3:00 AM IST 6 hours remaining November 4, 2026 - 9:00 AM IST Submissions close November 4, 2026 - 12:00 PM IST Judging begins November 5, 2026 Winners announced Hackathon Duration: 36 hours Format: Fully online Registration: Free What CEREBRO Is About: CEREBRO is built around the intersection of AI and human emotion . Participants are encouraged to go beyond basic sentiment classification and explore how machines can understand changing emotional states across conversations, speech, and social interactions. Participants are free to choose their own programming languages, frameworks, models, datasets, and development approaches. The focus is on building a real, functional system rather than simply wrapping an existing AI API with a user interface. Who Can Participate? CEREBRO is open to students, developers, researchers, AI/ML enthusiasts, and anyone interested in building technology around emotion and sentiment intelligence. Teams can participate in the hackathon and work remotely from anywhere. title: Byteathon
organizer: Noorul Islam Center for Higher Education
description: BYTEATHON 2026 is a 24-hour innovation and technology hackathon organised by the Department of Computer Science and Engineering, Noorul Islam Centre for Higher Education (NICHE), Kanniyakumari. BYTEATHON brings together innovators, developers, programmers, designers, engineers, creators, and problem-solvers to transform real-world challenges into practical, innovative, and scalable solutions. Participants will work in teams to analyse problem statements, design solutions, select suitable technologies, develop prototypes, and demonstrate their implementation before an expert judging panel. The hackathon focuses on: Innovation and originality Technical implementation Problem-solving ability Functional prototype development Feasibility and scalability User experience Real-world applicability and impact Presentation and technical understanding With a ₹70,000 cash prize pool, an online preliminary round, and a 24-hour offline Grand Finale at NICHE, Kanniyakumari, BYTEATHON is designed to give participants an opportunity to build, experiment, collaborate, and demonstrate what they can create under real hackathon conditions. BYTEATHON 2026 at a Glance Event: BYTEATHON 2026 Organiser: Department of Computer Science and Engineering, Noorul Islam Centre for Higher Education (NICHE) Finale Venue: Noorul Islam Centre for Higher Education, Kanniyakumari, Tamil Nadu Format: Online Preliminary Round + Offline Grand Finale Grand Finale Duration: 24 Hours Team Size: 1-4 Members Eligibility: Open for everyone Inter-college Teams: Allowed Inter-specialisation / Inter-department Teams: Allowed Prize Pool: ₹70,000 Round 1 Submission Deadline: 2 October 2026 Grand Finale: 15 October 2026 Finalists: 30 Teams Round 1 Registration/Submission Fee: ₹400 per team Competition Format BYTEATHON 2026 will be conducted in two stages. Round 1 - Online Preliminary Round Round 1 is an online idea and solution submission round. Teams can choose from five curated problem statements or participate under the Open Innovation category. Participants are expected to identify the problem clearly, propose an innovative solution, explain its technical implementation, and demonstrate the feasibility and potential real-world impact of their idea. Round 1 Submission Requirements Teams must submit: 1. Presentation - 10 to 12 Slides The presentation should cover: Team details Selected Problem Statement / Problem Statement Code Problem understanding Proposed solution How the solution works Technology stack System architecture or workflow Innovation and uniqueness Feasibility Usability Real-world use cases Scalability and potential impact Key differentiators 2. Demo / Explanation Video - 3 to 5 Minutes The video should clearly explain: Selected problem statement Proposed solution Core idea and workflow Technical approach Technology stack Code or implementation overview, where applicable Feasibility Innovation Use cases What differentiates the solution from existing approaches 3. Prototype - Optional for Round 1 A prototype, mock-up, proof of concept, repository, or demonstrable implementation may be submitted where applicable. While a complete prototype is not mandatory for Round 1, teams capable of demonstrating technical progress are encouraged to do so. Round 1 Deadline : 2 October 2026 All submissions must be completed before the announced deadline. Submissions will undergo a multi-stage evaluation process, after which 30 teams will be shortlisted for the BYTEATHON Grand Finale. Round 2 - 24-Hour Offline Grand Finale The shortlisted teams will be invited to participate in the 24-hour offline BYTEATHON Grand Finale at Noorul Islam Centre for Higher Education (NICHE), Kanniyakumari. Grand Finale Date: 15 October 2026 To maintain fairness among all finalists, teams will receive the applicable final-round problem statements/challenges as instructed by the organisers for the Grand Finale. During the 24-hour hackathon, teams will: Analyse the challenge Brainstorm and design their solution Develop the system architecture Build and integrate components Test their implementation Develop a functional prototype Prepare their final presentation Demonstrate the solution before the judging panel At the end of the hackathon, every team must present a working prototype or demonstrable implementation and explain its architecture, technology stack, design decisions, functionality, feasibility, limitations, and potential real-world impact. Judges may question teams regarding any part of their implementation to verify their understanding and contribution. Problem Statements BYTEATHON Round 1 consists of: 5 Curated Problem Statements 1 Open Innovation Track Teams may select one of the provided challenges or participate through Open Innovation where applicable. The challenges are designed around real-world problem-solving, technology, innovation, software development, engineering, AI, cybersecurity, automation, digital solutions, and practical applications of emerging technologies, depending on the individual problem statement. Participants are encouraged to develop solutions that are: Technically sound Innovative Practical User-focused Feasible Scalable Impactful Detailed problem statements, requirements, templates, and submission instructions will be available through the official BYTEATHON communication channels and platforms. Who Can Participate? BYTEATHON is open for everyone who wants to build, innovate, and solve problems. Participants with backgrounds or interests in areas such as the following are welcome: Computer Science Information Technology Artificial Intelligence & Machine Learning Data Science Cybersecurity Electronics Robotics Engineering UI/UX Design Web Development Mobile App Development Cloud Computing IoT Automation Product Development Entrepreneurship Design Innovation Participants do not need to restrict their teams to a single discipline. Team Rules Each team can consist of 1 to 4 members. Solo participation is allowed. Inter-college teams are allowed. Inter-specialisation and inter-department teams are allowed. Participants from different academic years may form a team. Cross-disciplinary teams are encouraged. A participant may be registered with only one team. Each team must nominate one member as the Team Leader. Participant details submitted during registration must be accurate. Identification may be requested by the organisers wherever required for verification. Evaluation Criteria Projects may be evaluated based on: 1. Problem Understanding How clearly the team understands the selected challenge and its underlying requirements. 2. Innovation and Originality The uniqueness, creativity, and novelty of the proposed approach. 3. Technical Implementation Quality of architecture, engineering, programming, integration, algorithms, technologies, and implementation decisions. 4. Prototype Functionality How effectively the prototype demonstrates the proposed solution. 5. Feasibility Whether the solution can realistically be implemented, deployed, maintained, or expanded. 6. Real-World Applicability The relevance of the solution to practical problems and real users. 7. Impact Potential social, technological, commercial, environmental, institutional, or user impact, depending on the problem. 8. Scalability Ability of the solution to grow beyond the prototype stage. 9. User Experience Usability, accessibility, interface design, and overall experience where applicable. 10. Presentation and Demonstration Clarity and effectiveness of the team's final presentation and live demonstration. 11. Technical Understanding The team's ability to explain, justify, debug, modify, and defend its own implementation during interaction with the judging panel. Participants may use: AI coding assistants Generative AI tools Open-source libraries Frameworks APIs SDKs Development environments Public datasets Cloud platforms Design tools Automation tools Publicly available technical resources However, participants must understand the solution they submit. However: Their use must be disclosed wherever applicable. Previously developed components used by the team must be declared. Teams must clearly distinguish between existing components and work developed specifically for BYTEATHON. External resources must not be misrepresented as original work created by the team. The focus of evaluation will be on how effectively the team designs, integrates, implements, and understands its complete solution. Plagiarism and Originality The solution submitted must represent the genuine work and contribution of the registered team. The following may result in disqualification: Copying another team's solution Submitting another person's project Submitting an existing project without disclosure Plagiarism Misrepresenting third-party work as original Falsifying implementation or results Using prohibited resources where restrictions have specifically been announced The organising committee and judges may conduct technical verification wherever necessary. General Rules Participants must complete registration before the specified deadline. Participants may compete only as part of their registered team. Team members should not be changed after the registration deadline without prior approval from the organisers. A participant cannot represent more than one team. Teams must work on only one selected problem statement or Open Innovation submission unless otherwise instructed. All required submissions must be provided within the specified deadlines. Late or incomplete submissions may not be evaluated. Participants must follow the prescribed submission format. Teams are responsible for ensuring that submitted presentation links, video links, repositories, documents, prototypes, and other materials are accessible to the evaluation panel. Offensive, unlawful, deliberately harmful, unsafe, or unethical projects may be rejected or disqualified. Participants must maintain professional conduct throughout BYTEATHON. Harassment, deliberate damage to property, misconduct, or violation of institutional rules may lead to disqualification. Final-round participants are responsible for bringing their own laptops, chargers, development environments, adapters, and specialised personal equipment unless specifically stated otherwise. Internet access, mentoring facilities, or other resources offered by the organisers will be subject to availability. Participants are responsible for maintaining appropriate backups of their work. Teams must comply with venue and institutional regulations during the offline Grand Finale. Judges may evaluate both the final product and the team's understanding of how it was built. The decision of the judging panel and organising committee will be final. The organising committee reserves the right to modify the event schedule, rules, problem statements, judging process, or competition format where reasonably necessary. Important changes will be communicated through official BYTEATHON channels. Prize Pool - ₹70,000 BYTEATHON 2026 features a total cash prize pool of ₹70,000. Winner - ₹40,000 1st Runner-Up - ₹20,000 2nd Runner-Up - ₹10,000 Winners will be selected by the official judging panel according to the announced evaluation criteria. Certificates and other recognition or opportunities associated with BYTEATHON will be communicated through official event channels. Finalists and Grand Finale A total of 30 teams will be shortlisted from the preliminary round for the offline Grand Finale. The BYTEATHON 24-Hour Grand Finale will be conducted at: Noorul Islam Centre for Higher Education (NICHE), Kanniyakumari, Tamil Nadu Food and accommodation for eligible finalists during the final event will be provided by the organisers as per the arrangements and instructions communicated to shortlisted teams. Important Dates Round 1 Submission Deadline : 2 October 2026 24-Hour Offline Grand Finale : From 15 October 2026 Why Participate in BYTEATHON 2026? BYTEATHON is more than an idea competition. It is an opportunity to: Build a real working prototype Solve real-world challenges Test your technical and problem-solving skills Work with developers, designers, engineers, and innovators Experiment with AI and emerging technologies Gain hands-on hackathon experience Present before an expert judging panel Compete for a ₹70,000 prize pool Build your portfolio and project experience Network with participants, mentors, industry professionals, and innovators Turn an idea into something that actually works Whether you are a developer, designer, engineer, cybersecurity enthusiast, AI/ML builder, entrepreneur, product thinker, or simply someone with a problem worth solving, BYTEATHON gives you 24 hours to turn your thinking into reality. Welcome to BYTEATHON 2026!

title: The Sequential Matching Problem
description: The Sequential Matching Problem: Romeo & Juliet × IIT Madras An Applied Machine Learning Programme & Hackathon How should a system decide who should be introduced to whom when it does not know everything about the people involved, feedback arrives over time, and each decision changes the options and information available later? The Sequential Matching Problem explores this question through an applied machine learning programme focused on matching, recommendation systems, optimisation and sequential decision-making . The programme is designed to go beyond a conventional hackathon. Participants will first explore the challenge through workshops and research before moving into implementation, experimentation and mentorship. The Challenge: The challenge explores how intelligent systems can make matching decisions when information is incomplete, feedback changes over time, and each decision can affect what happens next. Participants will explore questions such as: How should a system make decisions with incomplete information? How should it respond when feedback arrives over time? How should uncertainty be handled? What information is worth acquiring? How should different possible outcomes be compared? How can a system make decisions that remain effective as conditions change? The programme brings together ideas from machine learning, recommendation systems, optimisation and sequential decision-making . Participants will work with a controlled environment using synthetic data, allowing them to experiment with these ideas without using real-world personal data. How The Programme Works: The programme is structured across three stages. 1. Workshops & Research: 5 to 11 October 2026 The first stage focuses on learning, research and technical reasoning. Participants will attend technical sessions, explore the challenge and work with their teams to develop their approach. Teams will investigate: Problem interpretation Technical assumptions Modelling approaches Decision strategies Uncertainty Experimental design Potential limitations and failure cases Teams will then submit their research and proposed approach before moving into the build phase. 2. Build & Mentorship: 12 to 18 October 2026 Selected teams will move into the implementation phase. Teams will gain access to the development environment and turn their ideas into working systems. During this phase, teams will: Implement their approach against the simulator Compare their approach with supplied baselines Run experiments and ablations Investigate performance under different conditions Study the effects of incomplete, noisy or delayed information Take part in technical mentorship and office hours Prepare a reproducible final submission 3. Final Evaluation: Following the build phase, selected teams will enter the final evaluation process. Systems will be evaluated in controlled environments, including private environments that are not identical to the public development environment. This is designed to assess how well an approach generalises beyond the development setting. Finalists will also present their work and answer technical questions about their approach, experiments and findings. The Development Environment: The competition will use a Python-based sequential simulator with documentation and baseline examples. The simulator provides a controlled environment where teams can make decisions, observe outcomes and study how their systems behave over time. The underlying outcome-generating process will remain hidden from participants. Data & Privacy: The competition uses synthetic data throughout . Participants will not be asked to provide dating, relationship or compatibility information. No real Romeo & Juliet member data will be used. Participants retain ownership of the code, models, reports and other work they submit. Participation does not transfer ownership of a submission to Romeo & Juliet. Romeo & Juliet retains ownership of its own platform, technology, materials and work developed by or for the company before, during or after the programme. Participation, or a similarity between a submission and Romeo & Juliet's work, does not give a participant ownership of Romeo & Juliet's independently developed work. If Romeo & Juliet wishes to use a participant's submitted work in its product, the parties will discuss that separately and agree the terms in writing. Who Can Participate?: The programme is open to students from IITs across India . Eligibility: Any year of study Any academic discipline or degree programme Teams of 1 to 4 students You do not need to be enrolled in a formal machine learning course. Participants should be comfortable with at least one quantitative or technical area such as coding, mathematics or data analysis . Recommended Preparation: The following are recommended, but not mandatory: Python Basic probability and statistics Introductory machine learning Students from computer science, data science, mathematics, physics, engineering, economics and related disciplines are encouraged to participate. Programme Timeline: Phase Dates Registration & Team Formation 25 Sep to 2 Oct 2026 PS Release 5 Oct 2026 Workshops & Research 5 to 11 Oct 2026 Build & Mentorship 12 to 18 Oct 2026 Final Evaluation After 18 Oct 2026 Final Presentations & Judging Date to be announced Format: Fully remote Team Size: 1 to 4 students Data: Synthetic throughout What You Will Submit: Round 1: Research & Approach Teams will develop and submit their proposed approach, covering areas such as: Problem interpretation Key hypotheses Proposed modelling approach Decision or allocation strategy Treatment of uncertainty Learning strategy Planned experiments Relevant baselines Expected failure modes Build Stage: Selected teams will submit: Working implementation Source code or repository Reproducible environment Experimental and ablation results Comparison against supplied baselines Short technical report Final Submission: Finalists will be expected to provide: Final reproducible system Technical report and experimental analysis Private evaluation execution Presentation or demonstration Technical Q&A GitHub repository URL Workshops & Technical Learning: The programme will explore topics across applied machine learning and technical decision-making. Reciprocal Matching & Recommendation Systems: Two-sided recommendation, directional outcomes and the difference between ranking pairs and allocating across a pool. Learning From Noisy & Incomplete Data: Missing information, uncertainty, sparse observations and cold-start scenarios. Optimisation Under Constraints: Global matching, constrained optimisation and computational trade-offs. Exploration, Exploitation & Online Learning: Selective feedback, information value and sequential learning. Building Robust ML Systems From Messy Data: Experimental design, validation, reproducibility and failure analysis. From Technical Model To Real Product: Connecting technical performance with practical constraints and user value. How Will Teams Be Evaluated? Evaluation will consider the quality and performance of the systems developed throughout the programme. Areas may include: Technical performance Matching and allocation quality Handling of uncertainty and incomplete information Robustness Experimental quality Research reasoning Reproducibility Detailed evaluation criteria will be provided as part of the competition documentation. Beyond The Hackathon: The programme also provides an opportunity to connect with the technical team at Romeo & Juliet . Selected participants may be considered for paid internship opportunities with Romeo & Juliet. Internship consideration may take into account technical work, independent problem-solving, experimentation, scientific and engineering judgement, ability to explain technical trade-offs and subsequent technical discussions or interviews. Exact internship terms will be communicated separately once finalised. Registration: There Are Two Steps To Complete Your Registration Step 1: Register On Unstop Create or join your team on Unstop. After forming or joining your team on Unstop, proceed to the official event website and complete the registration process. You will provide the required participant and team information and complete a short interaction with Juliet , Romeo & Juliet's AI onboarding agent. The interaction takes approximately five minutes and consists of six questions. There are no right or wrong answers.

Stage 8 | Final Results: The highest-performing teams will be selected based on the overall evaluation. Final results will be announced after completion of the evaluation process. Hackathon Format: Stage Format Registration Online Assessment Online Team Shortlisting Based on applicable criteria Problem Statement Released digitally Development 7 Days - Fully Remote Submission Online Project Evaluation Evaluation Panel Final Results Based on Competition Performance Recognition Selected Participants/Teams What You Need to Build: Once your team is selected for the main challenge, you will receive a problem statement describing a real-world challenge. Your objective is to transform that challenge into a functional, thoughtful, and practical solution . Competition Rules: Participation: Each participant can register with only one team . Each team must have 2-4 members . Team members may belong to different colleges, cities, or institutions. Late submissions may not be considered. Teams may be required to provide a repository, deployed application, demo video, documentation, presentation, or other materials specified by the organizers. Integrity: Plagiarism, impersonation, falsification, or submission of another team's work will result in disqualification. title: Prompt Run 2026
description: PROMPT RUN: Prompt. Build. Run. PROMPT RUN is a 6-hour, fully online, individual Web Development Vibe Coding Hackathon focused on modern web technologies, rapid product development, creative problem-solving, and effective use of Vibe Coding workflows. Participants will receive a challenge and must independently transform the given problem statement into a functional, modern web application within the 6-hour hackathon period. This is not a traditional team hackathon. Every participant competes individually , builds their own project, submits it for automated evaluation, and competes on the official leaderboard. Hackathon Format: Duration: 6 Hours Mode: Fully Online Participation: Individual Domain: Web Development Format: Vibe Coding Evaluation: FAIE Automated Evaluation Engine Ranking: Official Leaderboard Submission Chances: 3 Participants will receive the challenge at the beginning of the event and will have six hours to plan, build, test, improve, and submit their solution. Vibe Coding: PROMPT RUN is designed around modern Vibe Coding and rapid development workflows . Participants can use AI-assisted development tools and modern development platforms to accelerate their workflow and transform ideas into working products. Participants may use: AI coding assistants Vibe Coding platforms Modern frontend frameworks Component libraries UI and design systems Animation and interaction libraries APIs and web services Development and debugging tools Other relevant modern web development tools The focus is on how effectively participants can understand the challenge, develop a solution, iterate on their idea, and deliver a functional product within the given time . Modern Technology Requirement: PROMPT RUN is specifically focused on modern web development . Participants are required to use a modern framework, library, or technology stack to build their project. Examples of acceptable technologies include: React Next.js Vue Nuxt Svelte SvelteKit Angular Astro Remix TypeScript-based modern frameworks Modern UI/component libraries Modern CSS frameworks and styling systems Frontend animation and interaction libraries Modern backend and API technologies where required Participants are free to choose the technology stack that best suits their solution. Standalone Technologies Are Not Permitted as the Primary Stack: Raw HTML-only projects Raw CSS-only projects Vanilla JavaScript-only projects Static HTML/CSS/JavaScript websites without a modern framework or technology stack HTML, CSS, and JavaScript may naturally be generated or used internally by modern frameworks, but the project itself must be built using a modern web development stack . Three Submission Chances: Every participant gets 3 submission chances during the hackathon. These three chances allow participants to improve and refine their project during the event. Participants can: Build → Submit → Evaluate → Improve → Resubmit However, there is an important rule: The Latest Submission Is Always Considered: The final score will be calculated from the latest valid submission made by the participant. The highest score among the three submissions will not be automatically retained. Example: Submission 1 - 72 points Submission 2 - 86 points Submission 3 - 79 points The final considered score will be: 79 points because Submission 3 is the latest valid submission. Participants should therefore use their three chances strategically and ensure that their final submission represents their strongest version. FAIE - Automated Evaluation Engine: PROMPT RUN uses FAIE - Frontend Arena Intelligent Evaluation Engine to automatically evaluate submitted projects. FAIE is an automated evaluation engine based on predefined evaluation criteria and technical checks . It is not an AI judge. The same evaluation process is applied to participant submissions according to the defined hackathon evaluation framework. FAIE evaluates multiple aspects of the submitted project, which may include: UI/UX Quality Functionality Performance Code Quality Responsiveness Accessibility Problem Statement Alignment Overall Technical Implementation After evaluation, FAIE generates a score for the submitted project. Live Leaderboard: PROMPT RUN features an official leaderboard where participants can track their current ranking. After a submission is evaluated: Submission → FAIE Evaluation → Score → Leaderboard If a participant submits again, their previous submission is replaced by the latest valid submission for leaderboard purposes. Therefore, the leaderboard always reflects the participant's latest valid evaluated score . The leaderboard will be used to determine the final results of the hackathon. Final Positions: Rank #1 - WINNER Rank #2 - RUNNER-UP Rank #3 - SECOND RUNNER-UP The final winners will be determined according to the official final leaderboard ranking . How PROMPT RUN Works: 01 - Start: Receive the hackathon challenge and understand the problem statement. 02 - Prompt: Use your preferred Vibe Coding workflow and development tools to plan and build your solution. 03 - Build: Develop a modern web application using an eligible technology stack. 04 - Submit: Submit your working project for automated evaluation. 05 - Evaluate: FAIE automatically evaluates your submission and generates your score. 06 - Improve: Use your remaining submission chances to refine your project. 07 - Climb: Your latest valid score is reflected on the official leaderboard. 08 - Finish: When the submission window closes, the final leaderboard determines the winners. Rules & Guidelines: PROMPT RUN is an individual participation hackathon. Team submissions are not allowed. The total hackathon duration is 6 hours . The event is conducted fully online . The project must be related to web development and must follow the given challenge. Participants must use a modern web development framework, library, or technology stack . Raw HTML-only, CSS-only, or Vanilla JavaScript-only projects are not permitted as the primary project stack. Vibe Coding and AI-assisted development tools are allowed. Participants may use their preferred modern frameworks, libraries, APIs, development tools, and supporting technologies. Participants receive 3 submission chances . Every new valid submission replaces the previous submission for leaderboard purposes. Only the latest valid submission will be considered for the final score. The highest score among the three submissions will not automatically be retained. All submitted projects will be evaluated through FAIE - Frontend Arena Intelligent Evaluation Engine . Participants must ensure that their submitted project is functional and accessible for evaluation. Projects should be developed within the official hackathon duration. Participants may use publicly available documentation, libraries, frameworks, and development resources. Participants must not submit plagiarized or substantially copied projects. Any attempt to manipulate the evaluation engine, leaderboard, submission system, or scoring process may result in disqualification. Participants are responsible for testing their project before making their final submission. Submissions made after the official deadline will not be considered. Participants must comply with all technical and submission requirements specified by the organizers. The final results will be determined according to the official final leaderboard . The organizers reserve the right to disqualify submissions that violate the rules or compromise the integrity of the competition. Who Can Participate?: PROMPT RUN is open to: Students Web Developers Frontend Developers Full-Stack Developers UI/UX Designers Vibe Coders AI-assisted Developers Technology Enthusiasts Anyone interested in modern web development, Vibe Coding, rapid prototyping, and building digital products can participate. The Challenge: Participants will be given a specific problem statement at the start of the hackathon. Your task is to understand the challenge and build a creative, functional, and modern web solution within six hours. The project should demonstrate: Clear understanding of the problem Creative solution design Strong UI/UX Functional implementation Modern technology usage Effective development workflow Attention to performance and usability Final Result: The competition follows a simple progression: BUILD → SUBMIT → FAIE → SCORE → LEADERBOARD Every participant gets three chances to improve their project. But remember: Your latest submission is the one that counts. At the end of the hackathon, the final leaderboard will determine the winners. One Participant. Three Chances. Six Hours. One Leaderboard. PROMPT. BUILD. RUN.

Scoring should primarily use verified flags and published point values, with time used as a tie-break only where specified in advance. The event is intended for participants who want a technical and challenge-driven quantum experience, with clear instructions on permitted knowledge, tools and resources. A short qualifier or sample optimization task can be used to verify readiness before the main challenge. Evaluation can consider correctness, degree of optimization, resource usage, technical reasoning and compliance with stated constraints. The challenge is suitable for participants who have basic exposure to quantum circuits and Python/Qiskit and want to apply those concepts in a practical setting. Duration Total Duration: 90-120 minutes Rules & Guidelines Participants must compete individually. Participants will be provided with one or more quantum circuits for optimization. Solutions should be submitted within the allotted time. Participants may be required to provide the optimized circuit along with a brief explanation of the changes made. Evaluation may consider correctness, circuit optimization, resource usage, technical reasoning, and compliance with constraints . title: Game Jam - TantraFiesta 2026
organizer: Indian Institute of Information Technology (IIIT), Nagpur
description: Overview: The event is organized as a flagship competition of TantraFiesta 2026, the annual technical fest of IIIT Nagpur and one of the largest tech fests in Central India. It brings together game developers, designers, and innovators from across the country to showcase their talent. Registration Deadline: 5th October 2026 Online Round: 25th September 2026 - 5th October 2026 Finale Dates: 23rd October 2026 - 24th October 2026 Theme: Plot Twist Eligibility Criteria: The event is open to all students studying at any college/university in India. Timeline: Online Round: 25th September 2026 - 5th October 2026 Offline Round: 23rd and 24th October 2026 Game Jam Rules and Guidelines: Participants: The event is open to all students from any college or university. Inter-college/inter-university teams are allowed. There is no limit on the number of teams per college. Team size can range from 1 to 4 members. One participant can only participate in one team. Game Jam Format: The competition consists of two rounds: Online (Round 1) and Offline Finale (Round 2). You will receive the link to access the Game Jam through the email address you provided during registration. Alternatively, the link can be accessed through the Jam community WhatsApp group . The shortlisted teams from Round 1 will be invited for the Finals at the IIIT Nagpur campus. The Round 2 theme will be revealed on the day of commencement of Round 2. Game Parameters: Any game engine is allowed. The game should run standalone without requiring participants to download any external software. The game must be playable using only keyboard and mouse controls (for web or PC builds) or touch controls (for Android builds). The game must be published and submitted through the itch.io page and must comply with the submission criteria below. The game can be distributed to the audience without violating any licensing or terms and conditions of the game engine or the assets used. The game must not be a copy of any existing game; it should be unique. Participants are required to share the source code of their game through a Git repository. Judges' Decisions: Decisions of the judges and organizers are final and binding. Any public/free-to-use resource must be credited. The use of pirated assets and content will lead to disqualification. Asset Usage: Participants are allowed to use individual assets, provided they have the legal rights/licenses to use them. The use of full scenes or pre-made game prefabs is not allowed. For detailed guidelines, participants can contact the coordinators. The use of Generative AI is NOT allowed. All external assets MUST be credited properly. Finals (at IIITN Campus): The candidates will be given 24 hours to work on and perform the required modifications to their game. All finalist teams must reach the IIITN campus on or before the reporting time, i.e., 9 AM on 23rd October 2026. In case of arrival before 23rd October, finalists must either arrange their own accommodation or contact the organizers for accommodation in the Guest House (charges apply). Note: All participants are required to bring their own laptop/setup for the final round. Judgment Parameters (Round 1): Games will be evaluated based on the following parameters: Theme Adherance. Gameplay & Mechanics. Innovation & Creativity. Aesthetics. (Arts & Visuals) Sounds & Music. Enjoyment factor. The candidates will be informed of the results through the official TantraFiesta/Dimensions email on their registered email address, as well as through the WhatsApp group. Join the WhatsApp Group After Registering: https://chat.whatsapp.com/G5h3SNNn1qz7szH2faH7FI Judgment Parameters (Final Round): Will be announced on the day of the event. Submission Criteria: Submission Process: The first submission stage is online, where participants submit their game through the official Game Jam portal - itch.io/jam/tf-iiitn-game-jam-2026 Games must be submitted within the event's designated duration. The submission process requires documentation, including credits, assets, and the compiled game. Please upload a Git repository link that includes all the necessary game files. Shortlisted teams from Round 1 will be invited for the final round at the IIIT Nagpur campus. Participation in the offline round is mandatory to be eligible for prizes. Submission Format: The submitted game must be set as free so the judges can play and evaluate it. The entry will be considered invalid if the participant has not registered on Unstop. Game Overview: Provide a concise and engaging overview of your game, including its title, genre, and a brief description of the gameplay. Game Art and Graphics: Include screenshots, concept art, or gameplay videos to showcase the visual aspects of your game. Highlight any distinctive art style or design elements. Story and Narrative (If Applicable): If your game has a storyline or narrative, provide a brief synopsis without any spoilers. Controls and User Interface: Explain the control scheme for your game. Showcase the user interface and any innovative or user-friendly design elements. Technical Details: Provide technical information about the game engine, tools, and technologies used in development. Mention any performance optimizations and stability measures.
prize: 1st Prize: ₹20000 | 2nd Prize: ₹10000 | 3rd Prize: ₹5000

title: AppSurd'26: Code.Compile.Chaos
organizer: Indian Institute of Technology, Indian School of Mines (IIT ISM), Dhanbad
description: AppSurd '26: Code. Compile. Chaos. is a beginner-friendly app development hackathon conducted by the App Development Division of Cyber Labs - The Technical Society of IIT (ISM) Dhanbad. The event challenges participants to rapidly ideate, build, and pitch a functional cross-platform application based on an unconventional mystery prompt within a compressed 5 to 6-hour development sprint. Guidelines & Eligibility Eligibility: Open to all undergraduate and postgraduate college students interested in mobile application development, UI/UX design, and rapid prototyping. Team Size: Teams must consist of 2 to 3 members . Individual participation is not allowed. Inter-College Teams: Allowed. Team members can belong to different colleges/institutions. Inter-Specialization Teams: Allowed. Team members can be from different academic departments, branches, or years of study. Single Team Restriction: A participant can only register as part of one team. Technology Stack: Mandatory use of Flutter (cross-platform framework). Native Android/iOS or other cross-platform frameworks (React Native, KMP) are not permitted. Development Environment: Teams are responsible for bringing their laptops with pre-installed and tested Flutter SDKs, IDEs (Android Studio / Visual Studio Code), and physical testing devices or emulators. AI Assistance: AI coding assistants (e.g., GitHub Copilot, ChatGPT, Claude, Cursor) are permitted and encouraged for ideation, code generation, debugging, and learning. Process & Round Details Total Problem Statements: 6 Mystery Prompts There are 6 unique mystery challenge prompts prepared for the hackathon (ranging from hyper-focused utility tools to intentional anti-UX challenges). Each team will be randomly assigned 1 prompt during the reveal stage to build their application around. Stages & Duration Stage 1: Registration (Pre-Event) Duration: Open until the registration deadline. Details: Teams register on Unstop and configure their development environments. Stage 2: Opening Ceremony & Briefing Duration: 15 Minutes Details: Overview of hackathon mechanics, tech stack compliance, submission guidelines, and evaluation rubrics. Stage 3: Mystery Prompt Reveal Duration: 10 Minutes Details: Random prompt assignment to each team. Stage 4: Development Sprint Duration: 5 to 6 Hours Details: Live development phase. Teams build their working prototype using Flutter and AI tools. Stage 5: Project Submission Window Duration: 15 Minutes (prior to hackathon conclusion) Details: Submitting source code, runnable build (APK or Web link), slide deck, and AI usage summary. Stage 6: Presentation & Judging Round Duration: 3 to 5 Minutes Demo + 2 to 3 Minutes Q&A per team Details: Teams pitch their working app live to the judging panel and answer technical questions. Stage 7: Results & Prize Distribution Duration: 15 Minutes Details: Score consolidation, winner announcements, and certificate distribution. Competition Rules Stack Compliance: Applications must be built exclusively using Flutter. Submitting applications built on other frameworks will result in immediate disqualification. Fresh Development: All project code must be written during the official 5-6 hour development window. Submitting pre-existing projects, pre-built templates, or work completed prior to the prompt reveal is strictly prohibited. Disclosure of Pre-existing Assets: Any third-party open-source packages, public APIs, or basic boilerplates used must be disclosed during submission. AI Policy & Technical Comprehension: While AI coding assistants are allowed, participants must fully understand the codebase they submit. Judges will test participants' technical comprehension during the Q&A. Inability to explain AI-generated logic will result in heavy mark deductions under the Process evaluation category. Submission Deliverables: To qualify for evaluation, teams must submit all required assets before the submission deadline: Source code link (Public GitHub repository or Zip archive). Runnable application build (APK file or live Flutter Web URL). Presentation/Demo slides (PDF/PPT format). Written AI Usage Declaration (150-200 words). Presentation Compliance: Teams must stick strictly to the 3-5 minute presentation limit. Demonstrations must show a live working application; static UI mockups or video-only presentations will not receive full functionality marks. Fair Play & Integrity: Any form of plagiarism, code theft between teams, or deliberate misrepresentation of work will lead to immediate disqualification. Organizer Authority: Cyber Labs and the appointed judging panel hold the right to make final decisions on disputes, rule interpretations, and unforeseen contingencies. Evaluation Parameters (100 Marks Total) Criterion Marks Parameter Breakdown Product 25 Application functionality, stability, UI/UX execution, technical completeness, and Flutter implementation quality. Prompt Interpretation 25 Creativity, alignment with the randomly assigned mystery prompt, and originality of the solution. Presentation 25 Pitch clarity, effective live product demonstration, UI/UX explanation, and time management. Process 25 Technical understanding during Q&A, effective team collaboration, responsible AI integration, and workflow execution.
prize: Winner: ₹5000 | First Runner-up: ₹2500 | Second Runner-up: ₹1000

title: DevDash '26: Build. Break. Laugh.

description: What happens when you give developers a surprise idea and limited time to build it? DevDash '26: Build. Break. DevDash '26 - Build. Break. Laugh.

title: HackRobo 2.0
description: Overview: HACKROBO 2.0 is a 2-day national hardware hackathon that challenges undergraduate engineering students to design, build, and demonstrate innovative robotic solutions for a real-world environmental challenge. The 2026-27 edition focuses on Riverbank & River Cleaning Robots , with participants working on solutions that can operate in open water while reaching and retrieving debris accumulated along riverbanks. The hackathon encourages teams to combine mechanical design, electronics, embedded systems, robotics, and software to develop a functional prototype addressing the given problem statement. Date: 10-11 October 2026 No. of Days: 2 Days Duration: 36 Hours Members Count: 3-5 per team Eligibility: Undergraduate Engineering Students Inter-Specialization Teams: Allowed Mode: Offline Registration Fees: ₹2,000 per team Venue: Pillai College of Engineering, New Panvel East, Navi Mumbai Theme / Domain: Riverbank & River Cleaning Robots The hackathon focuses on developing robotic solutions for riverbank and river cleaning . Conventional aquatic cleanup systems primarily target floating waste in open water, while significant amounts of plastic and other debris accumulate along muddy riverbanks above the waterline. These areas can be difficult to access using conventional cleanup vessels. Participants are challenged to: Design a robot that can move through open water and reach riverbank debris without getting stuck. Teams are encouraged to explore solutions involving autonomous navigation, manual control, robotic manipulation, buoyancy, waterproofing, and stable operation near challenging shoreline conditions. Suggested Technical Approach Teams may explore a hybrid Autonomous Surface Vessel (ASV) incorporating: Dual-Mode Control: Autonomous GPS/waypoint navigation for open water with manual RC override near the shoreline. Articulated Arm: A 2-4 DoF robotic arm capable of retrieving debris without grounding the vessel. Power & Buoyancy: A stable and waterproof vessel capable of maintaining stability even when the arm is fully extended. Integrated Systems: Combination of mechanical, electronic, embedded, and software systems to achieve the required functionality. Event Format The event will be conducted over 24 hours across two days . Day 1: Registration, orientation, opening ceremony, hackathon commencement, mentoring, networking and jamming session. Day 2: Mentoring, final project submission, judging and winner announcement. Teams will work continuously on their prototypes during the hackathon. Mentors and volunteers will be available to provide technical guidance throughout the event. The detailed schedule is tentative and may be modified by the organizers. Judging Projects will be evaluated based on: Innovation Functionality Impact Presentation Working prototype/demonstration A functional working prototype is strongly encouraged for the final evaluation. Facilities & Perks On-campus accommodation Meals throughout the event Workspace access Mentorship from industry experts Networking opportunities Participation certificates Winner recognition Industry exposure Opportunity to build a real hardware prototype Rules & Guidelines: Teams must consist of 3 to 5 members . Inter-specialization teams are allowed , provided all members are undergraduate engineering students from the same institution. Participants must work on the designated Riverbank & River Cleaning Robots domain. Teams are expected to develop and demonstrate a functional robotic solution to the given problem statement. Teams must complete and submit their project within the specified hackathon timeline. Teams must follow all instructions provided by the organizers and mentors. Only approved resources may be used during the hackathon. Participants must maintain fair play, discipline, and professional conduct throughout the event. Teams must be available for mentoring and evaluation rounds as scheduled. The final project must be submitted before the final judging round. Judges may evaluate the project based on innovation, functionality, impact, and presentation . Any violation of the event guidelines or engagement in unfair practices may result in disqualification. The event schedule is tentative and may be modified by the organizers if required. Decisions made by the organizing and judging committee regarding the competition will be considered final. Prize Pool: ₹75,000 The prize pool will be distributed among the top-performing teams, along with possible special recognition awards. Why Participate? Build a real-world hardware solution Gain hands-on experience in robotics and engineering Work on an environmental challenge Receive mentorship and technical guidance Network with students, mentors, and professionals Gain industry exposure Strengthen your engineering portfolio Earn certificates and recognition Experience an intensive 24-hour hardware hackathon HACKROBO 2.0 is an opportunity to move beyond ideas and build, test, and demonstrate a real robotic solution to a real-world problem.
prize: Prize Pool: ₹75000

title: Ignite Series - Open Innovation Challenge
description: Think. Build. Pitch. IGNITE. IGNITE Series - Open Innovation Challenge is a 15-day innovation competition organized by the Startup & Entrepreneurship Club, Chandigarh University , where students get the opportunity to transform their ideas into structured, market-ready solutions. Unlike conventional competitions with predefined problem statements, IGNITE gives participants the freedom to choose a problem they genuinely want to solve and develop their own innovative solution. From identifying a problem to validating the market, developing an MVP, designing a business model, and presenting the idea through a pitch deck - participants are encouraged to approach their idea like a real startup. Eligibility Open to Students from Colleges and Universities Across India . Team Size: 2-6 Members Inter-College Teams Are Allowed Inter-Specialization / Interdisciplinary Teams Are Allowed Students from Different Academic Backgrounds Are Encouraged to Collaborate. Each Participant Can Be a Member of Only One Team . How It Works Competition Duration: 15 Days The Complete Challenge Will Take Place Through the Startup & Entrepreneurship Club's Official Platform . Step 1 - Register Teams Register for The Ignite Open Innovation Challenge . Step 2 - Develop Your Idea Teams Identify a Real-World Problem and Develop Their Proposed Solution. Participants Can Work on Areas Such As: Domains AI & Technology FinTech Cybersecurity Healthcare Sustainability Education Business & Startups Social Impact Logistics And Much More! Step 3 - Submit Teams Submit Their Innovation Along with The Required Information, Including: Problem Statement Proposed Solution Target Market Market Validation Mvp / Prototype Business Model Go-To-Market Strategy Pitch Deck Step 4 - Edit & Improve Teams Can Edit and Update Their Submission at Any Time Before the Competition Deadline . This Allows Participants to Continuously Improve Their Idea, Mvp, Business Model, and Pitch Based on Their Progress During the 15-Day Challenge. ️ Once the Submission Deadline Passes, No Further Modifications Will Be Allowed. Step 5 - Judging After the Submission Deadline, the Ignite Judging Panel will Evaluate the Final Submissions. All Teams Will Be Evaluated on A 100-Point Scale across Five Core Criteria. Step 6 - Results After Evaluation, the Results Will Be Announced by The Organizers. Winners and Selected Participants Will Receive Recognition and Certificates as Applicable. Evaluation Criteria Teams Will Be Evaluated by The Judging Panel on A 100-Point Scale across the Following Five Criteria: R1 - Team Alignment Maximum: 20 Points Evaluation Of: Co-Founder/team Compatibility ️ Balanced Skill Sets Technical + Business Capabilities ‍‍‍ Team Composition and Collaboration R2 - Market Size Maximum: 20 Points Evaluation Of: Significance of The Problem Customer/problem Validation ️ Customer Surveys and Interviews Tam / Sam / Som Analysis Market Opportunity R3 - ️ Mvp Execution Maximum: 20 Points Evaluation Of: Quality of The Mvp/live Demo Technical Implementation Design and Aesthetics ️ Ui/ux Execution Usability and Functionality R4 - Business Model Maximum: 20 Points Evaluation Of: Monetization Strategy Pricing Structure Go-To-Market Strategy Financial Model Scalability and Sustainability R5 - Pitch Deck Maximum: 20 Points Evaluation Of: Completeness of The Pitch Deck Conciseness and Clarity Storytelling Communication of The Idea Presentation Structure Total Score R1 Team Alignment - 20 R2 Market Size - 20 R3 Mvp Execution - 20 R4 Business Model - 20 R5 Pitch Deck - 20 Total: 100 Points Rules & Regulations Each Team Must Consist of 2-6 Members . Inter-College and Interdisciplinary Teams Are Permitted. Teams Are Free to Choose Their Own Problem Statement and Domain. All Submissions Must Be the Team's Original Work . Plagiarism, Copied Ideas, Fabricated Validation, or Misrepresentation May Lead to Disqualification. Participants May Use Ai Tools, Ap Is, Open-Source Technologies, and Third-Party Resources, but Their Contribution and Usage Should Be Appropriately Represented. Teams May Edit and Update Their Submission until The Official Deadline . After the Deadline, Submissions Will Be Locked for Evaluation. Judging Will Be Based on The 100-Point Evaluation Framework mentioned Above. The Judging Panel Will Evaluate the Final Version of Each Team's Submission. ️ the Decision of The Judging Panel Regarding Evaluation and Results Will Be Final. Participants Must Adhere to All Deadlines Communicated by The Organizers.

title: CyberQuest 2026

title: Hack N Build
description: About Hack N Build 2026 Hack N Build 2026 is a premier national-level hardware hackathon organized by Electronica, the official club of the Department of Electronics and Communication Engineering (ECE) at SRMIST, Delhi NCR Campus . Designed to bridge the gap between digital design and practical hardware execution, this competition pushes student teams from circuit simulation to building fully functional hardware prototypes live on campus . Prizes & Rewards Total Prize Pool: Cash prizes worth ₹50,000+ alongside exclusive tech goodies for top-performing teams . Certificates: National-level participation certificates for all registered teams and merit certificates for winners . Eligibility & Team Guidelines Eligibility: Open to all undergraduate engineering students . Team Size: Teams must consist of 3 to 5 members . Solo participation is strictly prohibited . Cross-Disciplinary Teams: Interdepartmental teams (e.g., combining ECE, CSE, IT, and Mechanical students) are highly encouraged . Registration Fee: ₹200 per team . Technical Tracks Participants must select or design a solution aligned with one of the four competition domains : Track 1: Smart Campus & Energy Management (IoT, Microgrids, Relay Protection) Track 2: MedTech & Assistive Wearables (Embedded Sensors, Haptic Feedback) Track 3: Robotics & Autonomous Systems (Rovers, Motor Drivers, Microcontrollers) Track 4: Open Innovation (AgriTech, Industrial Automation, Environmental Monitoring) Stages and Timeline Registration Phase: Closes on September 25, 2026. Round 1: Virtual Pitch & Ideation (Online) Date: September 26, 2026 Platform: Google Meet Format: Each team receives a 10-minute slot (7-minute pitch + 3-minute technical Q&A) . Deliverables: Present a slide deck detailing your problem statement, system block diagram, Bill of Materials (BOM), and CAD circuit model/simulation (TinkerCAD, EasyEDA, Proteus, Fritzing, etc.) . Bonus Points: Functional digital circuit simulations earn extra evaluation points . Selection: Top 20 to 25 teams advance to the offline final . Round 2: The Hardware Showcase & Final Build (Offline) Date: October 7, 2026 Venue: Peter F. Drucker Hall & Microprocessor Lab, SRMIST Delhi NCR Campus Format: On-campus build session, hardware assembly, circuit wiring, live testing, and prototype presentation to a panel of expert faculty judges . Evaluation Criteria Round 1 (Online): Technical Design & Simulation (50%), Innovation & Concept (30%), Presentation & Defense (20%) . Round 2 (Offline): Hardware Execution & Wiring (50%), Presentation & Defense (35%), Innovation & Concept (15%) . Important Rules & Guidelines Original Work: Projects must be built specifically for Hack N Build 2026 . Submitting pre-existing semester projects or pre-assembled DIY kits results in immediate disqualification . Know Your Build: Judges reserve the right to cross-examine team members on their codebase, microcontroller logic, and physical circuit paths . Hardware Requirements: Shortlisted teams must bring their own components, development boards (Arduino, ESP32, Raspberry Pi, etc.), laptops, and cables to the offline venue .

title: Code Noir Hackathon 2026
description: About the Hackathon: Explore the unknown. Engineer the unexpected. Code Noir is an open-ended hackathon where participants are challenged to look at problems differently and build solutions that are creative, useful, or unexpected. There is no fixed problem statement or specific domain . You can work on a problem you care about, improve an existing process, create a new product, experiment with technology, or explore an idea that you have always wanted to build. Whether it's AI, software, education, healthcare, finance, cybersecurity, productivity, social impact, entertainment, or something completely different - the choice is yours. Tracks: AI & Intelligent Systems Software & Developer Tools Healthcare & Wellbeing Education & Learning Finance & Commerce Social Impact & Accessibility ️Mobility & Urban Systems Cybersecurity & Privacy Productivity & Automation Open Innovation Tracks are provided for guidance only. Participants are free to build outside these categories. Why Participate? Build Without Limits: Choose any problem, idea, or opportunity you want to explore. Think Differently: Go beyond conventional solutions and experiment with fresh ideas. ️Turn Ideas Into Reality: Build a working product or prototype from scratch. Experiment with technologies and ideas without domain restrictions. Collaborate with developers, designers, AI/ML enthusiasts, and innovators. Build a project you can showcase in your portfolio. Get feedback from mentors and industry professionals. Connect with a growing community of builders. Eligibility: Students Software Developers Engineers AI/ML Enthusiasts Researchers Entrepreneurs & Startup Builders Open-source Contributors Professionals Anyone interested in building with technology Team Size: 1 - 4 members Event Format: Round 1 - Idea Submission: Start with an idea and demonstrate why it is worth building. Teams must identify a problem, opportunity, or user need and propose a product that addresses it. Submit a short PPT presentation covering: Slide 1 - Project Title, Track chosen, Team Name & Members Slide 2 - The Problem / Opportunity Slide 3 - Target Users & Why the Problem Matters Slide 4 - Your Proposed Solution Slide 5 - Existing Solutions / Current Approach Slide 6 - How It Works / User Flow Slide 7 - Technology Stack and Project Architecture Slide 8 - Basic Implementation Approach The strongest and most promising ideas will be shortlisted for the next stage. Final Round - Pitch & Prototype Demo The Top 15 shortlisted teams will proceed to the Final Round Each team will be required to submit a maximum 5-7 minute pitch video presenting their idea and demonstrating their working solution. The video should cover: Problem and target users Proposed solution Key features Technology and implementation Working product/prototype demonstration Impact and future scope The judging panel will evaluate how effectively each team has transformed their idea into a practical, innovative, and meaningful solution. The final evaluation will focus on: What you built, how well it works, how effectively it solves the problem, and the value it creates. The top 3 teams will be selected as the winners based on the final judging scores. Rules and Guidelines: Team size must be 1-4 members. Solo participation is allowed. Teams of 2-3 are recommended. Cross-college teams are allowed. Cross-disciplinary teams are encouraged. Participants can choose their own problem statement. There is no restriction on technology, framework, or programming language. Participants may build for any industry or domain. Teams must adhere to the event timeline and submission deadlines. Projects should demonstrate meaningful development during the hackathon. Any form of plagiarism, copied projects, or unfair practice will result in disqualification. Teams must clearly explain their problem, solution, implementation, and impact. The decision of the judges will be final and binding. AI tools and coding assistants are allowed. Judging Criteria: Problem Understanding - 15% Problem-Solution Fit - 20% Innovation & Originality - 15% Feasibility & Implementation Approach - 30% Impact & Value Potential - 10% Idea Explanation & Clarity - 10% Rewards: Top-performing teams will receive: Winner / Runner-Up Certificates for the top 3 teams Certificates of Merit for the top 15 teams Networking Opportunities Participation Certificates for eligible participants Open Source Recognition About Invoqe Invoqe is a student-built technology initiative focused on helping the next generation of builders learn by creating real products. We believe that the best way to develop engineering and problem-solving skills is to build, experiment, collaborate, and ship . Through hackathons, internships, mentorship, and hands-on projects, Invoqe creates opportunities for students, developers, and aspiring engineers to move beyond tutorials and build solutions to real-world problems.

title: AXION Hackathon
description: AXION HACKATHON - STAMPERS About the Hackathon STAMPERS presents AXION HACKATHON , a 24-hour online Open Innovation Hackathon powered by Unstop , bringing together students from different colleges, universities, branches and backgrounds to identify real-world problems and build innovative technology-driven solutions. AXION is designed to give participants the freedom to choose a problem that matters to them and transform their ideas into a functional prototype within 24 hours. Participants will get the opportunity to ideate, develop, test and present their solutions while collaborating with their teammates in an intensive hackathon environment. Event Details Event Name: AXION HACKATHON Organized by: STAMPERS Powered By: Unstop Date: 11 October 2026 Day: Sunday Duration: 24 Hours Mode: Online Theme: Open Innovation Team Size: 2-4 Members Registration: Exclusively through Unstop Eligibility The hackathon is open to college and university students . Students from recognized colleges/universities across India can participate. Students from any year of study are eligible. Students from any branch, specialization or academic discipline can participate. Students from Computer Science, Information Technology, Electronics, Electrical, Mechanical, Civil, AI/ML, Data Science, Management, Design and other disciplines are welcome. Inter-college teams are allowed. Inter-specialization/inter-department teams are allowed. Teams can consist of students from different colleges and different academic backgrounds. Participants must complete their registration through the official Unstop opportunity page. Team Formation Each team must have 2 to 4 members . A participant can be part of only one team . Inter-college teams are permitted. Inter-specialization teams are permitted. Teams may include members with different technical and non-technical skills. Every team must have a Team Leader . All team members must register individually on Unstop as instructed. Teams are responsible for ensuring that their team information is accurate. Hackathon Theme - Open Innovation AXION follows an Open Innovation format. There is no single fixed problem statement that all teams must solve. Instead, participants are encouraged to identify a genuine problem and develop an innovative technology-based solution. Possible areas include: Artificial Intelligence & Machine Learning Web Development Mobile Applications Cybersecurity FinTech EdTech HealthTech Sustainability Smart Cities Agriculture Climate & Environment Social Impact Accessibility Automation Blockchain & Web3 Internet of Things Data Science Productivity Campus Technology Other technology-driven domains Teams are free to choose their own domain as long as the project demonstrates a meaningful problem, solution and implementation. Hackathon Format The hackathon will be conducted for 24 continuous hours . Phase 1 - Ideation Teams identify a real-world problem and develop their initial solution concept. Phase 2 - Problem Definition Teams should clearly define: The problem Target users Existing challenges Proposed solution Why the solution is needed Phase 3 - Development Teams build their prototype/MVP during the hackathon. Phase 4 - Testing Teams test their solution, identify issues and improve their implementation. Phase 5 - Final Submission Teams submit their project and other required materials according to the official submission instructions. Phase 6 - Evaluation The submitted projects will be evaluated by the judging panel based on the applicable judging criteria. Number of Problem Statements AXION is an Open Innovation Hackathon . Therefore, there is no fixed number of problem statements . Each team will: Identify its own problem → Develop its own solution → Build a working prototype → Submit the project. Project Requirements Teams are expected to build a functional prototype, MVP or demonstrable implementation. Projects may include: Web applications Mobile applications AI/ML solutions Software platforms Automation systems IoT solutions Data-driven applications Hardware + software solutions Cybersecurity solutions Other technology-based innovations The final project should demonstrate a clear connection between the identified problem and the proposed solution. What Teams Should Submit Teams may be required to provide: Project Title Problem Statement Solution Description Key Features Technology/Tech Stack Project Demo Source Code/Repository , where applicable Project Presentation/Pitch Deck , if requested Demo Video , if requested Team Details The exact submission requirements and submission method will be communicated through the official Unstop opportunity and organizing team. Judging Criteria Projects may be evaluated on the following parameters: Innovation Originality and uniqueness of the idea. Problem Relevance How clearly the project addresses a genuine and meaningful problem. Technical Implementation Quality and effectiveness of the technology used. Functionality How effectively the prototype demonstrates the proposed solution. User Experience Usability, interface design and overall user experience. Impact Potential social, economic, environmental or technological impact. Scalability Potential for the solution to be expanded and used by a larger audience. Presentation Clarity of the team's explanation, demonstration and overall presentation. Rules & Regulations Registration for AXION HACKATHON must be completed exclusively through Unstop . Every team member must complete the required Unstop registration. Team size must be between 2 and 4 members . A participant cannot participate in multiple teams. Inter-college teams are allowed. Inter-specialization teams are allowed. Participants must join the official AXION WhatsApp group. Participants must follow all instructions communicated by STAMPERS and through Unstop. Participants must submit their projects within the announced submission deadline. Late submissions may not be accepted. Plagiarism and unauthorized copying of another team's work are strictly prohibited. Teams must not falsely claim ownership of another person's or organization's project. Teams may use open-source libraries, APIs, datasets and development tools, subject to their respective licenses. Teams should appropriately acknowledge significant third-party resources where applicable. Participants are responsible for ensuring that their project complies with applicable laws and regulations. Projects must not contain unlawful, harmful or malicious content. Participants must maintain professional and respectful conduct throughout the event. Any attempt to manipulate submissions, judging or registration information may result in disqualification. Teams must be able to explain their project and demonstrate their contribution. The organizing team reserves the right to disqualify participants or teams that violate the stated rules. The decision of the organizing/judging team regarding rule violations and evaluation will be final. Event schedules or procedures may be modified by the organizers when necessary, with updates communicated through official channels. Originality & Use of AI Participants may use commonly available development tools, frameworks, APIs, libraries and AI-assisted development tools. However, the team must understand and be able to explain the submitted solution. Using AI tools does not remove the team's responsibility for: Originality Code quality Project functionality Accuracy Proper attribution where required Compliance with third-party licenses Submitting a copied project or representing someone else's work as the team's own may result in disqualification.

Smart Community Health Monitoring for Water-Borne Diseases in Rural Areas Design an integrated solution for early warning and community health monitoring of water-borne diseases in rural areas. Smart Tourist Safety Monitoring & Incident Response System Design a complete system using AI, Geo-fencing, and Digital ID for tourist safety, especially in hilly or remote regions. Water-Borne Disease Early Warning System (Community Level) Design a system that monitors water quality and basic health indicators to provide early warnings for water-borne diseases. title: Hackyard Build 2026
description: Important: Complete Both Registration Steps To participate in Hackyard BUILD 2026, complete both registrations by 10 October 2026: Register on Unstop. Complete the official Hackyard BUILD 2026 registration at https://hackyard.org/build2026 . Both steps are required for your Hackyard BUILD 2026 registration to be complete. If you have already registered on Unstop, please complete Step 2 using the same email address so we can match your registration. Join the Hackyard Slack workspace for event updates and to connect with other participants : Join Hackyard on Slack About the Opportunity: Hackyard Build 2026 is a hybrid hackathon organized by Hackyard for developers, designers, innovators, and student builders to turn ideas into working technology solutions. The hackathon follows a two-round format: Round 1: Idea Submission: Participants will submit their idea and proposed solution online. Submissions will be evaluated based on problem relevance, innovation, feasibility, potential impact, and execution potential. Selected teams will be invited to the final round. Round 2: Grand Finale: Shortlisted teams will participate in the in-person final hackathon at IIT Guwahati. Teams will build a functional prototype, work collaboratively, and present their solution to a panel of judges. Registration for Round 2 is completely free. Selected participants attending the in-person round will only need to pay a nominal fee for food and accommodation. Projects will be evaluated by the jury on: Build: 40% Problem: 20% Ingenuity: 20% Potential: 20% Team Participation: Participate solo or form a team of 2-4 members (maximum 4). Teams may include developers, designers, researchers, entrepreneurs, and students from different backgrounds. Eligibility: The hackathon is open to students, developers, designers, innovators, and technology enthusiasts interested in building software-based solutions. Format: Round 1: Online | Idea Submission Round 2: Offline | IIT Guwahati | Final Hackathon Come with an idea, build with your team, and take it from concept to a working solution at Hackyard Build 2026. *Hackyard T-shirt Raffle️* Want to win an exclusive Hackyard T-shirt? Follow @the.hackyard on Instagram and share any Hackyard Build 2026 post on your Instagram Story. Make sure to tag @the.hackyard to enter the raffle! One lucky participant will win a Hackyard T-shirt! Frequently Asked Questions: Participation: What Is Hackyard Build 2026? A builder experience where ideas, problems, skills, and ambitious people come together to make something real. Are Applications Free? Yes. Applications are free, open to everyone, and run online from 14 September to 10 October 2026. Do I Need a Finished Product? No. Submit an idea, problem, or skill you would bring to a build. No finished product or polished pitch deck is required. If you already have a prototype, you can include a public link in the optional work-link field. What Happens After I Apply? Applications close on 10 October. The review window and selection-result date are still to be confirmed. Hackyard will contact selected builders with attendance details before travel. If you applied with a team, connect your team with a private team code after submitting. The physical build is at IIT Guwahati on 24-25 October 2026. Can I Participate Alone? Yes. Apply solo, with a team, or as someone looking for teammates. Every person submits their own application. Teams are connected with a private team code. How Do Team Codes Work? If you choose With a team, your team must have 2-4 people, with a maximum of 4. Submit your own application first. After submission, create a team to get a private code like HYB-7K4P2, or join an existing team with a code from a teammate. Everyone on the team must apply individually. Can I Connect My Team Later? Yes. If you do not have your team code yet, submit your application and connect the team later from your application status page. Your application remains valid without a connected team. Do I Need to Be a Developer? No. Building is not limited to code. Designers, researchers, operators, founders, and people with strong problem-solving skills are welcome. Building: Who Gets the $100 Hackyard LLM Credits? Every selected project gets one $100 LLM credit allocation from Hackyard. A solo builder receives the allocation directly; a 2-4-person team shares one allocation for its project. What Does Participant Mean? A participant is one individual applicant. You count as one participant whether you apply solo, apply as part of a 2-4-person team, or apply while looking for teammates. How Do Project Rewards Work for Solo Builders and Teams? A project means one competing build. A solo participant's build counts as one project, and a registered team of 2-4 participants shares one project. Project rewards are issued once per project, not once per person. Someone looking for teammates becomes part of the project they ultimately build; if they continue solo, their build counts as one project. What Can I Build? Anything worth building. Follow one of our suggested directions or build something completely your own. AI is a powerful building layer, not a requirement. Physical Build: Where and When Is the Physical Build? The physical build is a 24-hour hackathon at IIT Guwahati on 24-25 October 2026. Event entry is free. Travel to and from IIT Guwahati is not covered. Food and accommodation will be available at a participant fee; exact amounts will be shared with selected builders before travel. When Will Prizes Be Announced? Cash prize funding is not confirmed. Final prize details will be published only when confirmed.
