title: Grevix AfterCode
description: Grevix AfterCode is a 24-hour online solo hackathon built around one simple idea: One Builder. One Idea. 24 Hours. No Boundaries. Unlike traditional hackathons, participants are not given a fixed problem statement. You choose the problem you want to solve, decide what you want to build, and choose the tools and technologies you want to use. AI coding agents, APIs, no-code/low-code platforms, design tools, open-source technologies, and traditional development are all allowed. But there is a twist. During the 24-hour challenge, your original plan will be disrupted by unexpected challenges. The goal is not just to see what you can build. It is to see how well you can adapt when the plan changes. The AfterCode Challenge System The hackathon is divided into 3 phases of 8 hours each. Phase 1: Build Hours 0-8 Start with an idea you genuinely want to build. You decide: What problem you want to solve Who you are building for What your product should do Which technologies and tools you want to use How you want to approach the problem At the end of the first 8 hours, the first unexpected challenge will be revealed. Phase 2: Adapt Hours 8-16 Participants receive a Challenge Card containing a new requirement, constraint, or change. The challenge may require you to: Change your target user Modify or remove a core feature Change the intended use case Introduce a new interaction Work under a new constraint Rethink your original solution You decide how to respond. You can adapt your product, rebuild it, simplify it, or completely change your approach. At the end of the second 8-hour period, another Challenge Card will be revealed. The Challenge Cards will not be revealed before the hackathon. Phase 3: Rebuild & Ship Hours 16-24 The second unexpected challenge is introduced. You now have the final 8 hours to adapt your product, improve your solution, fix what matters, and prepare your final submission. At the end of 24 hours, your product must be ready to ship. Human + AI AI tools are allowed and encouraged. Participants may use AI coding agents, LLMs, APIs, AI design tools, and other AI-assisted development workflows. However, participants remain responsible for: Their decisions Their implementation Their use of AI-generated output Their final submission The core philosophy of AfterCode is: AI can help execute. The builder decides what actually matters. Eligibility Open to everyone Students, developers, professionals, freelancers, and independent builders can participate No specific college, degree, specialization, or programming background is required Participants can participate from any country, subject to applicable Unstop requirements Participation is strictly individual Team participation is not allowed No college, specialization, or team-based restrictions apply Technology Rules There is no mandatory technology stack. Participants may use: AI coding agents Large Language Models (LLMs) APIs No-code/low-code platforms Design tools Cloud services Open-source software Programming languages and frameworks of their choice Participants are responsible for complying with the terms of service, licenses, and usage policies of the tools and services they use. Submission Participants must submit their completed project before the final submission deadline. The submission may include: Project name and description Problem being solved Solution overview Working demo or live link, where applicable Source code or repository, where applicable Technologies and AI tools used Short explanation of how the project evolved through the AfterCode challenges Detailed submission instructions will be provided to registered participants before the submission window. Judging Criteria Projects will be evaluated using the following criteria: Problem Significance - 25% How meaningful and relevant is the problem being addressed? Creativity & Originality - 20% How unique, creative, and differentiated is the solution? Execution & Functionality - 25% How effectively does the product work, and how well has the idea been executed? Effective Use of Technology/AI - 15% How effectively are technology and AI being used to build and improve the solution? Real-World Impact - 15% What potential does the solution have to create meaningful real-world value? The amount of code generated will not determine the winner. Judges may also consider how effectively participants responded to the unexpected challenges introduced during the hackathon. Build Log Participants may be asked to document parts of their development journey through short checkpoints. Examples include: What did AI do? What did you decide? What did you reject? The purpose is to capture the human decision-making behind the final product rather than evaluating only the final output. Rules Participation is strictly individual. The project must be created during the official 24-hour hackathon period. Participants may use existing libraries, frameworks, APIs, and development tools. AI-assisted development is permitted. Participants must not submit someone else's project as their own. Plagiarism, fraudulent submissions, or deliberate misrepresentation may result in disqualification. Participants must respect the terms of service and licenses of all third-party tools and resources used. Participants are responsible for ensuring that their project does not violate applicable laws or third-party rights. Challenge Cards must be followed according to the instructions provided during the event. The final submission must be submitted before the official deadline. Grevix reserves the right to disqualify submissions that violate the event rules or demonstrate dishonest participation. Judges' decisions will be final. Event Structure October 11 → October 12, 2026 24 Hours Total 0-8 Hours: Build 8 Hours: Challenge 1 8-16 Hours: Adapt & Build 16 Hours: Challenge 2 16-24 Hours: Rebuild & Ship 24 Hours: Final Submission The AfterCode Philosophy No fixed problem. No fixed technology stack. No predetermined solution. Just one builder, one idea, and 24 hours to see how far you can take it. Build. Adapt. Rebuild. Ship. Join the Grevix AfterCode Community Join the official Grevix AfterCode WhatsApp Group for announcements, updates, challenge information, and event communication. https://chat.whatsapp.com/H393VGmO0jQFLmtbifgh1w?s=cl&p=a&mlu=4&ilr=4 Grevix AfterCode 2026 One Builder. One Idea. 24 Hours. No Boundaries.

title: Solve - a - Thon | National Hackathon
organizer: Swami Rama Himalayan University (SRHU), Baksar Wala, Uttarakhand
description: Overview: AI for Sustainable Development Goals (AI for SDGs): Solve-a-Thon 2026 is a National 24-Hour Hackathon organized by the Department of Computer Science and Engineering, School of Science & Technology (SST), Swami Rama Himalayan University (SRHU), Dehradun, Uttarakhand. Scheduled for 27-28 November 2026, Solve-a-Thon is designed to bring together student innovators, programmers, AI/ML enthusiasts, developers, researchers, and multidisciplinary problem-solvers from across India to develop innovative technology-driven solutions for real-world challenges aligned with the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). The hackathon focuses on the theme "AI for SDGs", encouraging participants to explore the use of Artificial Intelligence, Machine Learning, Data Science, Software Development, and other relevant emerging technologies to address challenges in areas such as Healthcare, Education, Climate Action, Agriculture, Smart Cities, Governance, Clean Water, and Open Innovation. Solve-a-Thon is designed as more than a conventional coding competition. It provides participants with an opportunity to identify a meaningful problem, develop an innovative solution, build a functional prototype, receive technical guidance, and demonstrate their work before an expert evaluation panel. The Solve-a-Thon Challenge: The challenge is simple: Identify a real-world problem. Build an innovative technology-driven solution. Demonstrate how your solution can create meaningful impact. Participants will work in teams to transform their ideas into functional prototypes, applications, models, or demonstrable proofs of concept. The hackathon emphasizes not only coding and technical implementation but also innovation, problem relevance, feasibility, practical applicability, social/environmental impact, scalability, and the team's understanding of the proposed solution. Hackathon Themes: Participants can develop solutions under any of the following themes: AI for Healthcare: Develop innovative AI-powered solutions addressing healthcare challenges, patient support, health monitoring, diagnostics, preventive healthcare, accessibility, and related real-world healthcare needs. AI for Education: Build intelligent solutions that can improve teaching and learning, personalized education, assessment, educational accessibility, student engagement, and other challenges in the education ecosystem. AI for Climate Action: Use AI and emerging technologies to address climate-related challenges, environmental sustainability, monitoring, resource optimization, climate resilience, and awareness. AI for Agriculture: Develop technology-driven solutions for smart agriculture, crop monitoring, agricultural decision support, resource optimization, sustainable farming, food security, and other agriculture-related challenges. AI for Smart Cities: Create intelligent solutions for urban challenges including public services, mobility, infrastructure, resource management, citizen services, safety, sustainability, and other smart-city applications. AI for Governance: Explore innovative solutions that can improve public services, citizen engagement, administrative processes, accessibility, transparency, and data-driven decision-making. AI for Clean Water: Develop solutions addressing water quality, conservation, monitoring, contamination, distribution, sustainable water management, and other clean-water challenges. Open Theme: Have an innovative idea outside the listed themes? The Open Theme provides participants with the flexibility to identify a meaningful real-world problem and develop an innovative technology-based solution. Who Can Participate? The hackathon is open to eligible students participating through their institutions. Participants should have an interest or background in areas such as: Programming Artificial Intelligence Machine Learning Data Science Software Development Emerging Technologies Participants from multidisciplinary backgrounds are encouraged to form teams, bringing together different technical and domain perspectives to create stronger solutions. Team Size: Each team must consist of 3 to 5 members. Every team must nominate one Team Leader, who will be responsible for official communication and submission-related activities. Each team may also have one mentor to provide guidance and support during the hackathon. Mentor details are to be submitted to the Organizing Committee during registration. Hackathon Format: Solve-a-Thon will follow a two-stage process consisting of an initial online screening round followed by the main offline hackathon. Round 1 - Online Screening: Teams will first complete the prescribed registration process and undergo verification by the Organizing Committee. Registered teams will submit their problem statement in the prescribed HIMOVATION 2026 template within the announced deadline. The submitted problem statements will be evaluated by the designated evaluation panel, and eligible teams will be shortlisted for the next stage. Round 2 - Offline 24-Hour Hackathon: Shortlisted teams will be invited to Swami Rama Himalayan University (SRHU), Dehradun for the main hackathon. The offline stage will begin with an orientation covering the hackathon guidelines, rules, schedule, evaluation criteria, and other important information. Teams will then begin the development and coding phase and work continuously on their proposed solutions. The hackathon will include: Orientation Coding & Development Progress Review Overnight Development Final Submission Presentation & Demonstration Final Evaluation Teams will receive technical guidance and mentoring during the development phase. A progress evaluation will also be conducted during the hackathon to review the development status of participating teams. At the end of the 24-hour development period, teams will submit their completed projects in the prescribed format and present their final solutions before the evaluation panel. What Should You Build? Teams are expected to develop an original and innovative solution addressing a clearly identified problem. The final project may take the form of a: Functional prototype Application AI/ML model Software solution Demonstrable proof of concept Participants should clearly demonstrate: The problem being addressed The proposed solution How AI or relevant emerging technologies are being used Relevance to the selected SDG or real-world problem Technologies, tools, datasets, and frameworks used Working functionality or proof of concept Potential practical application and impact Teams must also ensure that their submitted work does not violate applicable intellectual property or copyright requirements. What Will the Jury Look For? Projects may be evaluated on the following parameters: Innovation & Originality: How innovative and original is the proposed solution? Problem/Theme Relevance: How effectively does the solution address the selected problem or theme? Technical Implementation: How well has the proposed solution been technically implemented? Use of AI/Emerging Technology: How effectively are AI or relevant emerging technologies utilized? Feasibility & Practical Applicability: Can the solution realistically be implemented and used? Social/Environmental Impact: What potential impact can the solution create? Scalability: Can the solution be expanded or adapted for larger-scale use? Prototype Quality: How functional, complete, and demonstrable is the prototype? Presentation & Demonstration: How clearly does the team communicate and demonstrate its solution? Teamwork & Understanding: Do team members demonstrate clear understanding of their solution and effective collaboration? 24-Hour Build Experience: Solve-a-Thon is a continuous 24-hour coding and development challenge. Teams will have to effectively manage their time between ideation, development, testing, debugging, documentation, and final presentation. Mandatory progress reviews will be conducted during the hackathon, and teams must remain prepared to demonstrate the progress and functionality of their solutions. The overnight development phase will provide teams with an opportunity to refine, test, and strengthen their prototypes before final submission. Food & Refreshments: During the hackathon, running tea and snacks during the daytime, along with dinner, will be provided to participants. Additional meals, refreshments, or personal food requirements will be the responsibility of participants. Food stalls will also be available at the venue on a paid basis. Rest Area & Hackathon Arena: Separate rest areas will be provided for male and female participants. Participants are required to follow the instructions of the Organizing Committee regarding the use of these facilities. For effective participation and monitoring, at least 50% of each team must remain present in the Hackathon Arena throughout the event. Rules & Responsible Participation: Participants are expected to maintain professional conduct throughout the hackathon. Solutions must be developed during the designated competition period, subject to the rules announced during orientation. Plagiarism and direct copying of another team's work are strictly prohibited. Teams may use publicly available libraries, frameworks, APIs, and datasets in accordance with their applicable licenses. Any external work, resource, dataset, or pre-existing component must be properly declared wherever required. Failure to submit the project within the prescribed deadline may result in disqualification. Teams must be prepared to demonstrate their working prototype before the jury. Prizes & Recognition: The total cash prize pool for Solve-a-Thon 2026 is ₹93,000. 1st Prize: ₹51,000 2nd Prize: ₹31,000 3rd Prize: ₹11,000 Winners will receive Certificates of Achievement along with the announced cash prizes. Registration: Registration Fee: ₹800 per team Teams must complete the registration process within the announced deadline. Registration details must include the names and institutional details of all team members. As per the hackathon guidelines, the initial online screening stage is conducted before the main offline stage. Teams participating only in Round 1 are not required to pay the registration fee at that stage. The applicable registration fee is required only for shortlisted teams proceeding to the subsequent stages, subject to the instructions and deadline communicated by the Organizing Committee. Registration will be confirmed only after successful payment and verification by the Organizing Committee. Event Details: Event: Solve-a-Thon 2026 - National 24-Hour Hackathon Theme: AI for Sustainable Development Goals (AI for SDGs) Date: 27-28 November 2026 Duration: 24 Hours Mode: Offline / On-Campus for shortlisted teams Venue: School of Science & Technology (SST), Swami Rama Himalayan University, Dehradun, Uttarakhand Team Size: 3-5 Members Registration Fee: ₹800 per shortlisted team Prize Pool: ₹93,000 Why Solve-a-Thon? Solve-a-Thon gives participants the opportunity to move beyond classroom exercises and work on problems that have real-world relevance. It is an opportunity to: Compete at a National-Level Hackathon Build an AI-powered solution for an SDG-linked challenge Work on a real-world problem within a 24-hour development environment Collaborate with a multidisciplinary team Receive technical guidance and mentoring Showcase a functional prototype before an expert jury Strengthen programming, AI, problem-solving, teamwork, and presentation skills Explore the practical application of emerging technologies Connect innovation with social and environmental impact Ready to Solve? You have 24 hours to turn an idea into a solution. Choose a problem that matters. Build something meaningful. Use technology intelligently. Demonstrate your impact. Think. Build. Solve. Impact.

Teams must balance speed, control, and defensive strategy to outmaneuver their opponents in a fast-paced knockout tournament - bringing their own robot, controller, and spare parts. Guidelines Team Size & Eligibility 2 participants per team Open to undergraduate/postgraduate students and eligible participants from colleges/institutions Valid college/institutional ID is mandatory Only registered participants may compete; one participant cannot be registered in two teams for the same event Team composition cannot be changed after the registration deadline without written approval from the Event Coordinator The registered team captain is the official point of contact Robot Specifications Specification Requirement Maximum Dimensions 350 × 350 mm (L × W) Maximum Weight 3 kg, including chassis, kicking mechanism, and batteries Maximum Voltage 3S LiPo, 12V DC/3s (fully charged) - IC engines, pneumatics, and compressors prohibited Control Fully wireless (RF or Bluetooth) manual control - no wired tethers, autonomous operation strictly banned Ball Handling At least 50% of the ball's surface must remain exposed at all times - mechanisms that fully trap, grab, suction, or swallow the ball are prohibited Pre-Event Inspection Teams must report to the arena at least 30 minutes before the official start time Every robot undergoes a technical inspection and weigh-in; robots failing weight, dimension, power, or ball-handling checks will be disqualified before the match begins Arena & Match Format Arena: 8 ft × 4 ft, with 60 cm wide goal posts on each side Single-elimination knockout format, with byes (for uneven team counts) assigned via random draw A standard match consists of 2 rounds of up to 90 seconds each; the ball starts at centre with robots inside their defence "D" until the referee's signal A round is won by the first team to score; if no goal is scored in 90 seconds, the round is tied A team wins the match by winning both rounds, or winning one and tying the other 30-second break between rounds, with teams switching sides If the ball goes out of bounds, play pauses, robots freeze in place, and the ball resets to centre A robot that completely stops working mid-round causes an automatic round forfeit for that team (it may still play the next round if repaired during the break) Tie-Breaker If tied after 2 rounds, a 3rd Tie-Breaker Round (max 90 seconds, first goal wins) is played If the 3rd round also ends 0-0, the winner is the team with the fewest accumulated penalties across all three rounds If goals and penalties are completely tied, judges decide based on Aggression and Control Judging Criteria Penalties are tallied (not awarded as free kicks) and used as a tie-breaker: Stalling (5-second rule): holding/pinning/trapping the ball in one position for over 5 seconds - 1 penalty point Goal camping (5-second rule): parking entirely inside your own goal for over 5 seconds without playing the ball - 1 penalty point Wall pinning (5-second rule): pinning the opponent against the arena wall while fighting for the ball for over 5 seconds - 1 penalty point Aggressive ramming: intentionally and repeatedly ramming the opponent instead of playing the ball - 1 penalty point Hand touches: manually resetting a flipped/stuck robot - 1 penalty point each Disqualification The following will result in disqualification: Exceeding the published dimensions, weight, or voltage limits Using a wired controller or autonomous operation Ball-trapping/suction mechanisms that leave less than 50% of the ball exposed Deliberately damaging another team's robot Receiving unauthorized external assistance Cheating, misconduct, tampering with another team's equipment, or misrepresentation of identity Poor social conduct, misbehaviour, foul/abusive language, or intentional damage to the arena or opponent's robot The Event Jury/Referee/Technical Committee holds final authority on match decisions, technical eligibility, penalties, disqualification, scoring, rule interpretation, and safety decisions. Right to appeal: penalized teams may present their case to the Event Coordinators, but the administration's verdict is final. NOTE-: Registration Fees are not refundable.

title: Digital Twin Challenge 2026
description: The future of medicine is proactive, not reactive. At the upcoming Happiest Health Reimagining and Reforming Healthcare in India Summit - 2026, Bengaluru , we are exploring the frontiers of digital health, focusing heavily on the concept of the Digital Twin. A Digital Twin in healthcare is a dynamic, virtual replica of a patient, constantly updated with real-time data from wearables, paired with Electronic Health Records (EHR). By simulating a patient's unique physiology, it can predict adverse health events before they happen and personalize treatment protocols. We are inviting the brightest minds from India's top university incubators to build the foundational prototypes of this future. We challenge student teams to build a proof-of-concept (PoC) Digital Twin Model focused on predicting a specific, localized health outcome. Because building a complete, whole-body Digital Twin is beyond the scope of a short-term project, teams must select one specific chronic or lifestyle condition prevalent in India (e.g., Type 2 Diabetes, Hypertension, or Cardiovascular risk). Eligibility Open to students interested in AI, healthcare, data science and digital health, including students from relevant technical, medical and interdisciplinary backgrounds. Team Formation Guidelines: A team will consist of 1-4 students, and the one who registers the team will be the team leader. Inter-college and interdisciplinary teams can participate. Only full-time students can participate. All the team members are required to verify and confirm their details to form a team. There is no restriction on the number of individuals/teams from an institute. Modification of team post registration will not be allowed. Two members from each of the finalist teams will need to travel to Bengaluru to present their solution in front of an audience at the summit. (Happiest Health will sponsor travel and stay) Phases of the Challenge: Phase 1 - Prototype & Code Submission The teams build their Digital Twin proof-of-concept and submit the completed project with required documentation as specified in the submission guidelines below under GitHub repository. Submitted solutions are evaluated by the technical and expert panel. Top 5 teams will be finalized by the jury, and an email communication will be sent to top 5 shortlisted team by Happiest Health The prototype must successfully demonstrate the fusion of two data streams: Static/Historical data: Simulated Electronic Health Records (demographics, past diagnoses, lab results, genetic markers). Dynamic/Real-time data: Simulated or open-source time-series data from consumer wearables/IoT sensors (heart rate variability, continuous glucose monitors, sleep stages, step count). The output: A working algorithmic model that ingests these two streams and successfully predicts an adverse event (e.g., predicting a sudden glucose spike 2 hours in advance, or flagging a high-risk cardiovascular anomaly based on a week of sleep and heart-rate data). Teams must also present a conceptual UI dashboard showing how a doctor would interact with this virtual patient. Navigating data constraints (The sandbox rules) We recognize that access to real patient data is restricted by privacy laws like the DPDP Act and HIPAA. Teams are strictly required to use anonymized, open-source, or synthetic datasets for training their models. For EHRs: Teams may use synthetic patient generation tools (like Synthea) or anonymized clinical databases (like MIMIC-IV). For sensor data: Teams may utilize open-source wearable datasets or generate their own synthetic time-series data mimicking Apple Health, Google Fit, or dedicated medical IoT devices. Submission Guidelines : Submit the project through a public GitHub repository link. Include all the details mentioned below in the README file of the repository. Team details and college/incubator information Project Title Problem statement and healthcare use case Technical stack, AI/ML model or framework details Minimum 2-5-minute video explaining and demonstrating your prototype. The video can be recorded as a PowerPoint presentation or uploaded as an unlisted YouTube video. Open-source license details Architecture diagram in PDF/PPT format Presentation in PDF/PPT format with project details and outcome Submission Instructions Folder name: Team Name_College Name Set the GitHub repository link access to Public, Ensure that all files and links are accessible to the evaluation team. Submit only the Team leaders name, phone number, email id and Public GitHub repository link on the submission platform. Phase 2 - Final Jury Presentation After the initial screening, the top 10 teams will present their solution and demonstrate their working prototype to the expert jury virtually, showcasing both the technical implementation and real-world healthcare impact. Phase 3 - Summit Showcase The top 5 teams will be invited to present their solution at the Reimagining and Reforming Healthcare in India Summit 2026, Bengaluru, on 20 November 2026. Winners will be announced following the final evaluation. Travel and stay for two members from each team will be sponsored by Happiest Health. Rewards & Opportunities Grand Finale winners/winning team will receive INR 1 lakh cash and a certificate. 1st Runner-Up/1st Runner-Up team will receive INR 50,000 cash and a certificate. 2nd Runner-Up/2nd Runner-Up team will receive INR 30,000 cash and a certificate Two teams will receive a Special Recognition Award of INR 10,000 each. The winning teams will earn PPI Opportunities to intern with Happiest Health.

title: NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026
description: Guidelines: Eligibility: Open to students, developers, engineers, scientists, designers, researchers, and innovators. Participants from all academic disciplines and specialisations are eligible. Participants from different colleges/universities can form a team. Inter-specialisation and multidisciplinary teams are allowed and encouraged. Participants can participate individually or as part of a team. Participants must complete the required registration process before participating. Team Formation: Inter-college teams are allowed. Inter-specialisation teams are allowed. Participants can collaborate with members having different technical and non-technical skills. Teams should select one official NASA Space Apps Challenge problem statement. Competition Format: This is a two-day international hackathon . Participants will select one official NASA Space Apps Challenge problem statement. Teams will research the problem, develop a solution/prototype, and present their work. Solutions may involve software, hardware, data analysis, scientific research, engineering, design, visualisation, storytelling, or other innovative approaches. Participants can use relevant NASA and Space Agency partner open data and resources. The completed project must be submitted through the official submission process within the specified deadline. Problem Statements: Multiple official problem statements will be provided by NASA on the 28th of October Each team must select one challenge statement. The number and detailed descriptions of the 2026 problem statements will be released through the official NASA Space Apps platform. Duration: 14-15 November 2026 Duration: 2 Days The detailed local event schedule, including registration, development, mentoring, submission, and presentation timings, will be communicated by the organising team. Process: Register for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026. Form a team or participate individually. Select one official challenge/problem statement. Understand and research the selected problem. Identify and use relevant NASA open data and resources. Develop an innovative solution or prototype. Test and refine the solution. Prepare the project documentation and presentation. Submit the final project within the specified deadline. Projects will be evaluated according to the applicable NASA Space Apps judging criteria and process. Rules: The project must address an official NASA Space Apps Challenge problem statement. Participants must comply with the official NASA Space Apps rules and terms. All external data, software, libraries, images, and other resources used in the project must be appropriately acknowledged or cited. Participants must have the necessary rights and permissions to use materials included in their submission. Projects must be submitted within the specified hackathon timeline. Plagiarism and unauthorised use of another participant's or team's work are not permitted. Participants must maintain professional and respectful conduct throughout the event. Any form of harassment, discrimination, bullying, or misconduct is prohibited. Teams are responsible for the originality, accuracy, and legality of their submissions. The organisers reserve the right to disqualify submissions that violate the event rules or official NASA Space Apps terms. The decision of the organisers/judging panel, in accordance with the applicable event rules, will be final. Participants should regularly check the official event communication channels for updates regarding schedules, submissions, and other requirements

title: Students of Global Impact
organizer: International Foundation for Sustainable Peace and Development
description: Overview Students of Global Impact - Social Startup Championship India's largest student-driven nation-building initiative The Social Startup Championship, presented by IFSPD Europe (Special Consultative Status, United Nations ECOSOC), invites student founders across India to solve real problems and build the nation. Open to all students, the championship recognizes young changemakers who turn ideas into action - from grassroots community projects to scalable social ventures. Every Founder who applies gets certified. Top founders advance to a fully funded, 3-day residential summit, where they compete for national awards and university certification alongside India's most promising student innovators. Highlights: Open to all students, no prior experience required. Every applicant receives official certification as a Founder. Top-performing founders are invited to a fully funded, 3-day residential summit - meals, stay, and networking included. Winners receive national recognition and a university certificate programme. Get your Founder Pass at PortAhead Application deadline: 30 September 2026 Details of the Opportunity: Students of Global Impact - Social Startup Championship is India's largest student-driven nation-building initiative, presented by IFSPD Europe (Special Consultative Status, United Nations ECOSOC). It invites student founders to design and execute a real-world action project addressing a UN Sustainable Development Goal (SDG) of their choice - not a hypothetical pitch, but a project actually carried out and independently verified. Every founder who registers and submits a verified project is certified. Verified founders earn points and badges as they progress through five levels - Founder → Rising Founder → District → State → National → Global Founder. Founders who reach the top levels are invited to a fully funded, 3-day residential summit, where they compete for national awards and a university certification. Guidelines: Eligibility: Open to all students, ages 12-21, studying at a recognized school or college in India. Team format: Individual or team entries. All team members must belong to the same college and the same field of specialization - inter-college and inter-specialization teams are not permitted. Team size: Up to confirm max team size, e.g. 4 members confirm max team size, e.g. 4 members . Format: Open-ended - there are no fixed problem statements or timed rounds. Each founder/team selects one real-world problem aligned to any UN SDG and designs their own project to address it. Process: Register for a Founder Pass at PortAhead.com → execute the project → submit for review → project and impact are independently auditor-verified (self-reported claims alone are not accepted) → verified founders earn points/badges and progress through the levels. Duration: The project execution and submission window runs up to the application deadline of 30 September 2026; auditor verification and level progression continue on a rolling basis afterward. Summit eligibility: Founders verified at confirmthreshold,e.g.Nationallevelandaboveconfirm threshold, e.g. National level and above are invited to the fully funded, 3-day residential summit. Rules: One project per founder/team. The project must be original and not submitted to any other competition or platform. The project must be demonstrably linked to at least one UN Sustainable Development Goal. All team members must be from the same college and the same specialization/field of study; no inter-college or inter-specialization teams. Founder Pass registration at PortAhead.com is mandatory before a project can be submitted for verification. All claims of impact are subject to independent auditor verification. Fabricated evidence, plagiarism, or misrepresentation of results will result in disqualification. Decisions of the IFSPD Europe evaluation and auditing panel are final and binding. Registration and project submission must be completed by 30 September 2026.

title: Singularity 2.0
organizer: KC College of Engineering and Management Studies and Research
description: Overview Welcome to Singularity 2.0, the premier national-level hackathon where the conventional rules of technology break down! Born to cultivate a relentless building culture, Singularity 2.0 has evolved into a high-stakes arena for the brightest engineering minds across the country. This is an intensive, 18-hour offline sprint engineered to test your technical endurance, collaborative spirit, and execution. Forget basic tutorials and generic templates. At Singularity 2.0, you will step into a frictionless environment designed for one purpose: building disruptive, real-world solutions. What to Expect at Singularity 18-Hour Sprint: Build, test, and deploy under extreme time constraints. Elite Collaboration: Form cross-disciplinary teams to tackle real-world bottlenecks. Expert Mentorship: Get real-time guidance from industry experts. Production-Ready Builds: Transform ambitious concepts into fully functional prototypes. Participation Fee Singularity 2.0 is a paid hackathon . Shortlisted teams proceeding to the offline hackathon will be required to pay a ₹1,000 participation fee per team, irrespective of team size . Our Theme: The Technological Singularity In astrophysics, a singularity is a point of infinite density, often at the heart of a black hole, where the standard laws of physics completely cease to function. We have adopted this cosmic phenomenon to represent the rapidly accelerating frontier of the modern digital landscape. We are approaching a technological tipping point where artificial intelligence, automation, and interconnected networks are growing at an unstoppable, irreversible pace. This theme is a direct call to step across the event horizon. We challenge you to dismantle standard engineering paradigms and harness the raw power of our four core tracks: AI-Enabled Hardware, Health & Emergency Services, FinTech, and Environmental Technologies. Just as a physical singularity warps reality around it, this hackathon empowers you to warp the fabric of modern technology. At Singularity 2.0, you aren't just wiring hardware or writing lines of code; you are forging the architecture of tomorrow. Prepare to disrupt the status quo, engineer without constraints, and build the impossible.

title: Trivora
description: Overview TRIVORA 2026 is a national-level 24-hour hackathon presented by HackHere , bringing together students, developers, designers, researchers and technology innovators to build intelligent, scalable solutions using Generative AI and Cloud Computing . Event Details Dates: 5th & 6th December 2026 Duration: 24 Hours Theme: Generative AI × Cloud Mode: Offline Registration Fee : Rs 1000 per team Team Size: 1-4 Members Registration: Slot-based Key Highlights Cash prizes and exciting rewards Internship and career opportunities Exclusive AI and cloud credits Unique problem statement for every team Real-world technology challenges Industry mentorship and networking Certificates, recognition and partner benefits Opportunity to build and deploy a working product Hackathon Theme: Generative AI × Cloud Teams must develop innovative, intelligent and scalable solutions by combining the capabilities of Generative AI with modern cloud technologies . The solutions should demonstrate practical applications of AI, efficient cloud deployment, scalability, responsible data usage and measurable real-world impact. Unique Problem Statement Allocation Every participating team will receive a unique problem statement . All problem statements will follow the common theme of Generative AI × Cloud . Problem statements will be revealed at the beginning of the hackathon. Once allocated, teams cannot exchange or change their problem statement. Each team must independently design, develop and present its solution. Solutions must be developed during the official hackathon period. Why Participate? Build a working solution within 24 hours Solve a unique real-world problem Explore Generative AI and cloud technologies Gain hands-on product development experience Learn from industry mentors and professionals Access internship and career opportunities Receive exclusive technology credits and benefits Network with innovators from different institutions Showcase your skills on a national platform Eligibility & Team Rules Open to UG and PG students Students from all academic disciplines may participate Team Size: 1-4 members Inter-college teams are allowed Inter-department teams are allowed Multidisciplinary teams are encouraged Each participant may be part of only one team Hackathon Process Phase 1 - Problem Allocation & Ideation Each team will receive a unique problem statement. Teams must analyse the challenge and plan their proposed solution. Mentors may guide teams during idea validation. Teams must work only on their assigned problem statement. Phase 2 - Prototype Development Teams will develop their solution during the 24-hour hackathon. The solution should meaningfully use Generative AI and cloud technologies. Mentors and industry professionals will interact with participants. Teams may undergo progress evaluations during development. Phase 3 - Final Submission & Evaluation Teams must submit their final prototype and presentation. Shortlisted teams will demonstrate their solutions before the jury. Evaluation will focus on technical quality, innovation, scalability and practical impact. Submission Requirements Teams must submit: Working prototype or MVP Presentation deck Source-code repository Solution description Technology stack Cloud architecture or deployment details Demo or deployment link, wherever applicable Expected impact and scalability Evaluation Criteria Innovation and originality Effective use of Generative AI Cloud implementation and scalability Technical quality Functionality Relevance to the assigned problem Practical impact and feasibility Security and responsible data use Final presentation and demonstration
